Added flyable planes and helicopters (experimental, off by default, Options > Game > Flyable Planes, or the console commands plane and heli): climb into a plane of the Chicago airfield or one of two helicopters on the concrete apron, take off, fly around the city and land. The propellers and the rotors turn, with a faint disc when they run fast. Simple arcade flight with a chase camera, a small flight panel, an engine sound, and crashes into buildings and hard landings. Only the automatic flights (take off, climb, level flight, landing, hover, building crash, get in by the button) and pictures were checked, not the feel, the keys or the sound.

Rebuilt the third person cameras. On foot the right stick now orbits the camera round Tanner on a spring arm like Assassin's Creed (it builds up speed and brakes, it is not a flat pan, the camera follows behind after one and a half seconds, L1 moves it in over the shoulder, the picture gets wider while sprinting). Every camera outside the car (3rd Person, Cinematic, Lip, Rear Bumper, Front Quarter, Pole, Selfie Stick, Outrigger, Low Rear and the get in / get out shot) now keeps a clear view and is pulled in or moved when a building, wall, car or the ground is in the way. The Cinematic camera works like the one in GTA IV and V now: low street level shots (wide, low behind, beside, in front looking back, roadside pass-by, orbit when you stand), cuts every few seconds, a quick new shot after a crash, a drift or a jump, never above the roof line. Fixed the get in car camera that jumped below the ground. Checked by scripted drives in four cities and by pictures. The real pad feel and the cinematic camera by eye.

Changed the flyable planes and helicopters after the first hand check: the pilot is hidden while you fly (no more Tanner gliding under the plane), the plane banks the right way and the propeller stays on the nose, up arrow is nose up and left / right bank and turn (new option Invert Pitch), keys ramp smoothly, a flare assist and ground effect soften landings, the wheels hop on a firm touchdown, and the brakes stop it in about 100 m. The helicopter now has real gravity (new option Helicopter Hover Assist, on by default: off, it sinks, and a cut collective drops it to a crash), uses the escape helicopter model of the story read from your own Rio level, and turns and lifts with the right stick on a pad. A key and pad hint shows in the flight panel. Only the automatic flights, the pad axis test and pictures were checked.

Rebuilt the pop-up headlight pod. An open lid is now the cover on the back of a real lamp housing: a box with a left and right wall, a back, a bottom and a dark front with a lens that lights up with the headlights on, 12 triangles per lamp, deeper than before (0.8 of the lid side, 18 to 33 cm). The hole under the lid is a dark bucket with four walls and a floor, not one flat floor. Gran Turismo 1 cars show a plain lens panel. J key, the third of a second and the dusk ramp work as before. Pictures looked at: 180SX from the front, three-quarter, side, above and at lamp height, RX-7 FC, Eunos Roadster. The lens only shows as a thin strip from above because the lid opens about 60 degrees.

Changed the flyable planes and helicopters after the second hand check: the plane stick works like a flight stick again (up is nose down, the option Invert Pitch flips it), the craft and the camera now use the same blended position so the model stops shaking, and it is drawn without the world grain. You can get out at any time, also in the air: you bail out, a parachute opens by itself after 1.5 seconds and you survive the landing, the craft flies on without you and is put back about 20 seconds after it lands. The helicopter now shows the real texture of the escape helicopter, read from your own Rio level when you first fly it and kept in memory only. Only the automatic flights, the bail out and ground exit checks and pictures were run; the feel, the jitter and the parachute by eye are still open.

Rebuilt the pop-up headlight unit as a wedge like on a real 180SX (from a photo of a real 180SX): black housing, side walls are triangles that are tall at the front and flat at the hood, sloped top in the body colour, the lens a big rectangle on the front face, lit with the lights on. Same shape for every pop-up car (GT2 and GT1, 130 lids). The old lid plate and the thin glass strip are no longer drawn while the unit is up, so no stray leaf. The glow round the lamps of pop-up cars is dimmer and smaller (soft glow, not a white blob). Looked at pictures: 180SX, RX-7 FC, Eunos, MR2 from the front three-quarter, 180SX side, top and lamp height. The lens of the MR2 and some GT1 cars is dark or grey.

Rebuilt the Cinematic camera in two modes. DRIVE (what you get while you play, the default): 15 kinds of shot that all look forward over the road (near, far and high chase, over the shoulder, roof, over the hood, side, dolly, crane, sweep), each one checked every tick so you can always see where you are going, picked at random, held five to twelve seconds and always blended into the next in about a second without a hard cut (only after a crash). FULL SUITE: the whole film director set (low shots in front, three quarter, pass by, crane, dolly zoom, high shot, orbit when you stand still, whip pans, quick shots after crashes, drifts, jumps and near misses); it plays in the attract mode demos and with the auto director, or you pick it in Options > Controls > Camera > Cinematic Camera In Play (all languages, by hand). Fixed the jumps of the picture when a car drove between the camera and the car. Checked by scripted 3000 tick drives in four cities and by pictures.

Added far shots to the Cinematic camera while you drive, like GTA IV: a long lens from 40 to 100 metres, a roadside tripod that lets you drive through the frame, a high chase far behind, a side track from the street, a telephoto chase and a high overhead. They are about a quarter of the shots, the car is smaller but you still see the road ahead. Added a little handheld sway at speed, a lens that widens with speed, a small lean into corners, slow push ins, and an option Cinematic Shake (Off, Low, Medium, default Low) in all languages. Fixed the camera key not leaving the Cinematic camera (the test start switch forced it every frame). Fixed pops of the camera when a shot changed or an arm swept over a building corner. Only automatic tests ran.

Fixed the flown plane and helicopter. The d-pad now pitches like the arrow keys and the stick (up is nose down on the plane, forward on the helicopter). The chase view no longer shakes: it stopped following every nose wiggle and the plane model turns with the same blended angles as the camera. Checked by automatic tests,

Added the option Smart Racer AI (Options > People & Traffic, Advanced, off by default, experimental): the rivals of a street race are driven by the trained racer network instead of the traffic AI. They get the same 32 inputs as in training, back out of a wedge the same way, and the traffic AI takes the car again when the network file is missing or there is no route. Checked by automatic tests,

Fixed the split screen with two players cutting the car off: each player's view is a strip of half the window height, and the chase camera now stands further back so the whole car shows in every frame (measured: before, the car filled 73 percent of the strip and was cut off in every frame). Three and four players were already fine. Checked by a measurement log and by pictures.
Fixed the lit lens of a car to take the tint colour from the customizer: the glass of the headlights and the tail lens (the brake colour while braking) now change colour, not only the glow.
Fixed a moved head lamp to move its light beam on the road with it. Before, the beam stayed at the place the car came with.

Added amber rear indicators as the default for Gran Turismo cars whose tail lens has an amber patch (77 of the 1073 Gran Turismo 2 cars, like the Miata, Honda Beat and the Skyline R32). The converter writes the colour into the car's effects file, so the glow no longer shows red over the amber. Driver 1 and Driver 2 cars are not done yet.

Added pad control for the camera views of the customizer: hold both triggers (L2 + R2) and press the d-pad to pick the three quarter, front, side or rear view on every tab, also on the Car tab where the right stick button picks a random car. The key bar of the Car tab shows it, in all languages.

Added the option Smart Cop AI (Options, People and Traffic, Advanced view, off by default, experimental): the police cars in a chase are driven by the cop network of the Core pack instead of the original decision, and the original police AI drives again when the file is missing or refused. The network that ships passes the original decision through, so it drives like the original for now. Texts are in all languages. Checked by automatic tests,

Removed the name and tank table of the Driver 2 cars from the game: the tank now comes from the car file of the car, the name from the car catalog entry made from it, and a car without a file shows as Vehicle and has the tank of its length. All 39 table lines were compared with the car files before deleting them: equal. The geometry bake is described in MODDING_files. Checked by automatic tests,

Changed the help text of the Smart Cop AI option in all languages: it now says the police use a test network that drives like the normal police for now, because the network that ships only copies the normal police.

Made cars that wait to turn at yield signs stop only for a standing car that is within 5 m beside their path, not for the whole queue of the cross street in a 13 m wide window. In Havana that gave 29 percent more junction passages in a long test run and the cars wait less. Chicago is unchanged. Checked by automatic tests,

Added two sliders next to the Smart Racer AI and Smart Cop AI options (People & Traffic, Advanced view). Smart Racer Pace % makes the network rivals lift the gas now and then, so they are slower (30 to 100). Smart Cop Strength % mixes the network with the normal police driver (0 is the normal police, 100 is the network). Both are at 100 by default and then nothing changes. The texts are in all languages. Checked by automatic tests,

Made the police cars of the four Driver 2 cities the cities' own cruisers only. A Driver 1 cruiser could patrol Chicago, Havana, Vegas and Rio in half of the cases; now it never does. The five Driver 1 cities keep their own cruisers as before, and every other car stays free in every city. The old config key d1CopPercent is ignored (an old config.ini still loads); REDRIVER_D1COP only changes the Driver 1 cities now. Looked at pictures of a Chicago and a Havana chase: only the own cruisers. Checked by automatic tests,
Fixed the brake driving a car backwards when the tank is empty. A car with no fuel now only slows down and stays put when you hold the brake. Checked by automatic tests,

Fixed pedestrians that a car hit and that stayed standing and slid along stiff. The tumbling body only had 8 slots and they were never freed, so after a few hits the next one got none. There are 32 now and the slots of removed bodies are given back. The game logic is the same. Checked by automatic tests,

Fixed the racing wheel force feedback kicking like a crash in the first moment after a restart or a trip to another city: the speed of the old game was still remembered. The twin exhaust model lookup is forgotten with the car pool. Checked by automatic tests,

Made the traffic follow the clock. It is thin at night (5 percent of the maximum), grows through the morning, sits around a third at midday and is busiest from 4 to 7 in the evening (half of the maximum). Cars are never removed at once: new ones just stop appearing above the limit and far cars you cannot see go one per second. Added the option Traffic By Time Of Day (People & Traffic, on by default, in all languages by machine translation). Pedestrians keep their old curve. Checked by automatic tests,

Made the car customizer work for every player, one to eight. Each player opens it for his own car with his own pad, and keeps his own paint, wheel design, rim size, engine sound pick and My Cars list position. In a split screen the player who opens it gets the whole window while it is open. There is only one custom engine sound slot, so if two players pick a sound the last pick wins. Added a shop mode with the price beside every car, an Owned mark and a Buy button that takes the money from that player's wallet and puts the car in his My Cars list. The price is a stand in until the car economy is joined. Take a Drive works as before. Checked by automatic tests,

Added Gran Turismo road cars up to 1983 to the traffic. Up to 8 of them are picked when a city loads and stay loaded, so the traffic is the same on every run and no car loads in the middle of the game. The default list has 29 cars and can be replaced by a file. Checked by automatic tests, How the cars look in traffic, the frame rate.

Added the showroom door at the Auto Exchange on Goose Island: stand at the door (on foot or in a stopped car), press the action button and the car shop opens for you. It lists every car in the game with its price, cars after 1983 are marked and cost much more, and you pay from your own wallet. A bought car is yours and your old car stays in My Cars. Leaving without buying gives you your old car back exactly as it was, with its paint and damage. Checked by automatic tests with one player, two players and on foot. Two pads, how the prompt looks in split screen, the real door position. No display car and no test drive yet.

Fixed cars vanishing in front of you at a raised bridge in Chicago. They now stop before the bridge, wait in a line while it is up and drive on when it is down. Before, every car on the bridge road was removed the moment the bridge lifted, even a long way from the bridge. Checked by an automatic test with a forced raised bridge and a picture check, Cars that are already on the bridge when it rises are left alone if you can see them.

Stopped traffic from braking hard when you come up close behind it. Before, a car in front of you almost stopped (56 down to 11 km/h in a test) when you closed in from behind at 120 km/h, now it keeps its speed (no drop at 90, 120 or 160 km/h). Cars still brake for everything in front of them. Checked by automatic tests,

Added the shop's memory for lot cars: a car you took from the Auto Exchange lot is marked as stolen from the lot with your name on it. While it still exists the repair shop will not give you new plates (not for this one) and will not buy that car back (we know that car). Other stolen cars sell as before, and felony from other causes can be cleared as before. All languages, machine level. Checked by automatic tests,

Added Car Deformation (Options, Graphics, Effects, Advanced view, Off / Low / Normal, Normal by default): when a car hits a pole, a wall or another car hard, the body is pushed in around the spot that was hit, by about 7 to 20 cm, a little uneven, and more hits dent it more up to a limit of about a quarter of a metre. The glass and the underside give less and nothing tears. It only changes how the car looks: the crash, the damage and the collision boxes are the same as before. The repair shop makes the car clean again. Works on the traffic and the police too. Checked by automatic tests and pictures of a car hitting a bin at 80 km/h,

Made the car dents look like dents: the light on a pushed in body part now follows its new shape, and the dents stay on the car when its model is streamed in again. A hit on the side of a car now dents the door area and not the corner of the car. Repairing at the Auto Exchange takes the dents away, and two cars that hit each other both dent. Checked by automatic tests and pictures, and tried by hand with a wall hit at 20 and 80 km/h; the repair, car-to-car hits and the Off and Low options were

Added a stunt tracker to Take a Ride. Airtime, big jumps, flips, wheelies, near misses with other cars and drifts give small cash, and stunts close together make a combo that pays when it ends. A crash loses the combo. Best airtime and longest jump show on the Stats Records page. Ramp spots for jumps are in four city files. Only checked with fed test samples and automatic tests,

Made the stunt spot scan find real crests: it flies a car at 100 km/h off the height map of every road straight and keeps the places where it stays in the air. Every city now has 8 stunt jump spots (before 1 to 6).
Added two Take A Ride career numbers: the longest police chase and the car driven longest. Older stats files load as before. Unit test and checked on a sample profile,

Fixed the invisible stop on the Chicago water edge. A Driver 1 or Gran Turismo car stopped dead on the quay at x 22000 z -280832 because its collision box reaches a few units under the road and hit the top of the quay wall (type 279) that ends at road height. A level object box that ends under the road can no longer stop a car. The invisible fence slabs at the water edge (the original game's own) and the real fences still stop the car. I checked it with a scripted drive on the second PC (old rule stops the Driver 1 car, new rule passes, a Driver 2 car never stopped) and the tick hash set shows no change. Drive along the Chicago quay at x 22000 with a Driver 1 or Gran Turismo car, and look at the other cities (Havana, Vegas, Rio have 70, 28 and 54 such boxes).

Fixed custom wheels turning back into the city's grey wheels when the car speeds up (GitHub issue 11). The fast spinning wheel now gets the chosen rim smeared round its axis, in the design's own colours. The game builds. The test machine was too busy to make the customizer shots.
Fixed the car denting while invincible. The player car now takes no dents, and no damage marks, when invincibility is on. Only the build and the tick hash ran.

Fixed a police car that could work as a traffic car (a traffic rule could give the police car of another city a weight), and a traffic car that was spawned without a drawn model (the invisible car seen in Newcastle: such a pick is dropped now). The cause of the Newcastle car is a guess, it was not reproduced.
Added test and handbook for the 4096 car limit: a wide test car in the unit tests, a crowd scenario for the frame rate and the new limits in the modding handbook.

Fixed custom wheels turning back into the city's grey wheels when the car speeds up (GitHub issue 11). The fast spinning wheel is now painted with the chosen rim, smeared round the axle, in the design's colours. Looked at on a Driver 2 car, a Gran Turismo car and a Driver 1 car with the gold wheel, standing and at speed.
Fixed the cinematic camera swinging its view about 120 degrees for two seconds when it left a far roadside shot in front of the car. It cuts to the chase camera now.

Fixed incomplete roadblocks. A cap of three patrol cars counted the roadblock cars themselves, so a roadblock never had more than three cars, fewer with a patrol car around. A roadblock gets every car it has room for now: 4 in the first row on a 10 lane road in the test. The sim changes whenever a roadblock is built, so the tick hash of those scenes moves.

Cut back the collision boxes that reached 350 to 600 units past their drawn model: the ramp walls of Chicago and the roadworks pieces of Havana. A car on the road no longer stops against nothing there. The new numbers are a data file of the Core pack (collision/boxfix.txt), found by the hunter, and the logchecks fail when such a box is left on a road. Tried by tests only (the hunter finds 0 left in all four cities, tick hash: only mission 20 in Havana moves, as it should).

Fixed the weak stunt jump spots. I flew all 32 with the real car: the ones that gave only a short hop were moved to a better road crest or dropped, and a spot where the car just falls out of the map no longer counts. 24 are left (Chicago 8, Havana 2, Las Vegas 8, Rio 6), each flies 0.6 s or more and lands. Havana has only 2 because the city is too flat for more.

Fixed the hood view on cars with a higher roof. The camera point is now worked out from each car's body (foot of the windscreen, over the bonnet), so the bonnet shows on Driver 2, Driver 1, Gran Turismo cars, vans and trucks and the black wheel arches are gone. A car file can set its own point with a line 'hood x y z'. Looked at stills of 28 cars. (Driv3r cars not on this PC)

Added a Player Character option (Options > People and Traffic): on foot you can play Tanner of Driv3r, Tanner in his black suit, VortexLeStuntman or any of the Driv3r pedestrian models. Tanner of Driver 2 stays the default. The setup also makes Tanner of Driv3r from your own Driv3r disc. Walking, running, backwards and jumping have clips, car enter and exit still show a standing pose. Built and unit tested, not seen in the game yet.

Fixed the chase camera going black over a ramp or jump. When the map read a surface above the car (water over a gap, another road level, the map under a car that left it) the camera was pulled into the car and looked straight up. It now ignores a ground that is higher than the car. I found the cause with the stunt jump flights in four cities, not at the exact spot of the video. Test: cam_ramp_city0 to 3 and the camsweep unit test fail before the fix and pass after.

Fixed the Driv3r player characters. The black suit Tanner and VortexLeStuntman had a solid black head and Vortex a green and white striped body: the community models write their picture coordinates below zero and the game clamped them to one pixel row, so now they repeat into the picture when the model loads. Also fixed that the player on foot stayed the Driver 2 Tanner in free roam whatever character was picked: the check looked at a cutscene number that is -1 outside cutscenes, so it only worked after the first cutscene. New unit test chars3d_uvwrap (rule plus the two shipped models must have every corner inside the picture). Checked with pictures of both characters from four sides and the head close up, before and after, and tick hash;

Fixed the custom paint colour: it now stays on the car when I swap the car version, when I undo in the customizer and when I save the car in My Cars (new car.N.rgb field in the My Cars file). Unit test added to the My Cars test.

Fixed the chase camera dipping under the road on a crest, a bridge or a cliff road. The height limit of the camera was counted from the ground beside the car, so where the ground fell away the camera was dragged below the road the car drives on, and sometimes ended inside the car. It now counts from the road under the car. Checked with the stunt crest hunt in all four cities and the pictures of Chicago and Rio; the exact spot of the reported video is not found.

Made a police car borrowed from another city (Police Cars: Mixed) use the siren of its own city, and a Driver 1 cruiser show its single beacon. A script chase in Chicago and Frisco ran with borrowed cruisers pursuing.

Added Options > Graphics > Effects > Car Damage Look, Full or Off. Off draws every car without dents and without the damaged mesh, the damage itself and the crashes stay the same. In 21 languages. Checked by a log test and a picture,
Fixed the Chicago secret car showing the school bus model: the car drawing kept the bus buffer when the special car slot got the secret car. Checked by a log test, not by a picture of the car,

Added a tyre line to the car file, so a car can come with its own tyre compound (Race or Drift) unless you chose another in the garage. Race tyres now leave narrower, darker skid marks. Checked with the test bot on a Gran Turismo car (Race grips more, laps faster, Drift holds a slide) and the simulation hashes did not move. No car carries the line yet, and the Race marks were looked at only in test pictures.

Fixed the names of the Driver 2 cars in Choose A Ride and the pause menu car list. Model 0 is the police car in every city and the names sat one place off, so the Mercury Monarch showed the Oldsmobile and the other way round. The names follow the pictures now and the tanks stay with their car. The unit tests and the name audit passed, I did not look at the menus yet. The two pickups of Vegas and Rio are called Pickup because I do not know their make, and the order of the three Chicago cars still needs your eyes. Cars from an older install get the right names at once, the car files themselves only after the setup repair.
Fixed the chase camera ending up inside a building when the car falls out of the map (jump spots in Havana and Rio). The old camera was left where it was while the clear spot had already moved.

Saved the tyre compound (Normal, Race or Drift) of every player in the replay file, in a new trailer at the end of the file. A replay of a Race tyre drive now plays with Race tyres again, so the drive comes out the same. Old replays have no trailer and play with Normal tyres as before, and an older build skips the new bytes. Tested with a recorded Race drive and its replay on the second PC (the first 400 ticks equal) and unit tests for a cut off and a bad trailer.
Added a U-turn routine to the Smart Cop option: a cop swings round or backs out when you are behind it. It stays off by default, because the cop test round showed no gain beyond its noise.

I made the police car follow model 0 in the traffic rules. The Driver 2 police car is model 0 in every city (the cop voices and sirens already said so, and the car names were fixed to it last week), but the rules that tell the police car from the street cars still used model 3. Now the car kinds (Core city files, cars.kinds), the borrow weight, the foreign cop pick of Mixed police, the car sound / sheet / handling tables and their tests say model 0 = police and model 3 = a street car (Sebring, Delta 88, Cougar ...). So the traffic of every city now borrows the model 3 cars of the other cities, and the police car of another city still never drives as a civilian. The traffic and the cop choice change, so 147 tick hash scenarios moved.

Changed the Drift tyres so that only the throttle that reaches the rear wheels causes power oversteer: a front wheel drive car no longer slides its tail from the throttle, an all wheel drive car only with the rear share, rear wheel drive and cars without a sheet are unchanged. Measured on the tyre bed with a Golf V5 (front wheel drive): Race grips 13.8 percent more than Normal, the bot finds no throttle slide on Drift.

I gave the six Driver 1 police cars that all read Dodge St Regis Police (1979) a place in their name (San Francisco, Intro, Los Angeles, Los Angeles 2, New York, PC), and renamed the small Driver 1 coupe from Maserati Kyalami to Triumph Stag, because its model is a long nose fastback. The name tests pass; I did not look at the car list in the game.

Fixed: cars of the Ashland, Italian Job London and Driv3r Miami packs showed up in Chicago and every other city, low poly and half finished. Since 1302 the car scan took the built-in packs for the base set, so their city list and the pack switch were lost. They are traffic in their own city only now, and the scan counts them as packs again. Checked by a hidden Chicago run: 46 of these cars were picked before, 0 now in 424 picks.

Fixed three Rio cars that were filed under the wrong country in the traffic rules: the Mercedes 450 SL is German, the Thunderbird American and the Corcel Brazilian. The traffic shares of those cars in the American cities and in Rio change.

Hid the low poly Ashland taxi and van (wspc_taxi, wspc_bluevan) from the car lists as unfinished cars. They show again with Options > Gameplay > Show Unfinished Cars. The list is a small data file of the Core pack, so no car files have to be made again. The game log counts 3 unfinished cars now.

Fixed the invisible wall on State St in Chicago (public issue 14). The round light poles of the Goose Island lot are 262144 units away from State St, and the check that decides which editor boxes are near the car squared that distance in 32 bit, so the number wrapped and the poles passed as near. The car then hit them as walls that are not drawn. The distance is 64 bit now. A new test drives every lane of State St with the touch log on and fails on a hard stop or an editor box contact.

Dropped the traffic wish lines for Havana and Rio cars that no game file has a model for (Fairlane, Buick, Olds 88, Belvedere, Series 62, Falcon, Peugeot 404, Renault 4, the Soviet cars, Fusca, Brasilia, Opala, Chevette, Passat, Maverick, Polara) and removed the Known problem. The traffic in both cities does not change, those lines matched no car. Unit tests pass.

Made the Ashland cars an experimental group of their own in every car picker, like the GT1 and GT2 cars: an Ash tab in Choose A Ride, an Ashland source in the car browser and the customizer, an Ashland tab in the multiplayer picker, and "(experimental)" after each name (21 languages, machine translated). The taxi and the van are not hidden any more, all 17 stay selectable.

Added automatic lamp placement for cars (job CAR-LAMPS-FIT). The game reads the red tail lamp and amber indicator patches off the car model and its texture sheet and moves the brake, indicator and reverse points onto the real lenses; a point it finds no evidence for stays where the car had it, and a point that floats off the body comes from the shape of the body. Cars of the disc, mod and pack sets get it, the original Driver 2 cars keep their points. The tweak autolamps picks it: 0 is the old placement, 1 (default) all cars but Driver 2, 2 every car. A lamp point set in a car file still wins. Head lamps are NOT fixed where a car has no lamp glass row. Unit test and pictures only,

A wrecked car in Take a Ride is not the end any more, alone or online: the police stop chasing you, you step out and a new car of the same model waits where the wreck was (fine 100 dollars). Before it was game over or a restart. Option wreckrecovery in tweaks.ini (default on, 0 = the old game over). Races, events and game modes keep their own rules and get a hook, Events_PlayerWrecked. Tried by tests and two games on one PC with equal hashes,

Fixed the invisible wall on State St in Chicago. A pole of the Goose Island Auto Exchange is exactly 4 x 65536 units away from State St, and the distance test wrapped around in 32 bit numbers, so the far pole stopped cars as a box with nothing drawn. The distances are squared in 64 bit now. Driven by hand on State St in the dev copy, the wall is gone.

Fixed the rear wheels of the Dodge D250 pickup (Driver 1 PC) sitting far inside the body, and the front wheels of the Chevrolet Monte Carlo Landau. The setup now keeps the wheel track when the body skin it measures is just the inside of the wheel arch. Only these two cars changed in the full Disc Install, all other cars and all level files are byte equal. Tried by hand on the Dodge Ram in a freshly generated folder: the wheels look good. The Monte Carlo front wheels.

Fixed the name order of the car lists: numbers in a name now sort by value, so Sports Coupe comes before Sports Coupe 2 and Car 9 before Car 10, in Choose A Ride and in the car browser. Tried by the unit tests only,

Gave the Driv3r Miami cars their real in-game names (Packer Transport, Dart Retaliator, Flamingo Taxi, Police Prowler and so on), matched to each model by its picture. Car ids stay the same, so saves keep working. Tried by the unit test only,

Added the pipe style Modeled to the car effects: a pipe that is part of the car model draws nothing and the exhaust smoke starts at its tip. The Driv3r cars use it, so they get no generated exhaust pipe. Shows in the customizer Exhaust tab as Modeled pipe. Tried by the unit tests only,

Made more of the Driv3r Miami vehicles: the roadster (Velocity Turbo), the dump truck (Packer Transport), the box truck (Sobe Packer Truck), the bus, the work van and the tractor unit (Packer Big Daddy). The exhaust smoke of every Driv3r car starts at the tail pipes of its model. Tried by the unit tests and the converter on the disc only,

Changed the car you follow in the story chases to plow through traffic again without slowing down, like in the original, and throw the cars it hits into your way. It no longer passes through them like a ghost. It still passes buildings, takes no damage and is put back on its wheels after 2 s on its roof. No wreck, no crash, the same path as the original.

Added the option Solid Cars (People and Traffic): no car passes through another one in a crash or a traffic jam. The jam breaker no longer lets a stuck car drive through the cars around it, and cars that meet in a junction no longer pass each other. Players Only keeps the traffic helpers for the traffic and never ghosts a player; Off gives the original back. Jams about the same, a few percent fewer cars through the junctions, more traffic cars touch each other.

Pulled the tyres of the Driv3r Miami cars in so the flat tyre face no longer stands outside the body: the rear wheels of the coupe, fastback, luxury coupe, muscle coupe, sports coupes, racer, supercar and targa stuck out beside the rear quarters. The setup now fits each axle to the side of the body beside the wheel (at most 10 cm, cars that already looked right stay as they are), and the 13 changed car pictures are remade. Tried by the unit test, a disc install into a scratch folder and in-game pictures from behind, the side and above,

Fixed the washed out look of the Driv3r cars: they were squeezed into 16 colours per picture, now the setup keeps the original full colour textures (a 1024 picture next to every Driv3r, Ashland and London car file).

Gave the Driv3r cars their paint. The bodies came out white and grey because the real game tints them from a table of 16 paints per car that sits in the vehicle property files of the disc. The Disc Install now reads it and paints every car of Miami, Nice and Istanbul in one of its real colours, picked to match the in-game pictures of the wiki; taxis, police cars and buses keep the colours of their own pictures. The car pictures of all 55 cars were made again. The other 15 colours per car are decoded but not written yet. Tried by unit tests, a disc run in a scratch folder and pictures,

Pulled the wheels of the Driv3r coupes, Freddo, Dolch Schub and the Polis car further into the body, up to 14 cm instead of 10 cm, so the rear tyres no longer stand out of the fenders. All 55 cars were checked from behind, from the side and from above. Tried by unit tests and pictures,

Gave the Driv3r cars their wheel arches back. The Disc Install had cut away every triangle inside a box round each wheel, which took the arch lining and the fender lip with the baked tyres (30 to 190 triangles a car, up to 45 percent of what was cut). Now only the baked tyre goes, the arches stay, and the body is as wide at the fenders as on the disc. The wheel inset stays as it was on all 55 cars. Tried by unit tests, the disc stage and pictures,

Kept the hard edges of the Driv3r car bodies. The disc models carry a normal at every corner, but the converter dropped them and the car file smoothed over every shared vertex (6 to 12 degrees off on average, 3 to 5 percent of the corners over 45). The normals now go into the car and corners of a hard edge stay separate vertices. All 55 cars keep the full detail model (the work van is over the 4096 polygon limit and uses the lower one). Tried by unit tests, the disc stage and pictures,

Switched the car sheet physics on for every player: the package carries config/carsheet.ini (enabled, preset real), so the Car Realism row of the Game options page works (Real, Scaled, Capped) and Gran Turismo cars use their sheet. Before, only the dev folder had the file and a normal install showed 'Needs sheet physics (experimental)'. This changes the physics of the game for everybody, so every install needs the update to join online games together.

Fixed the release writing a file when F7 is pressed. F7 saved the player position as a gas station into config/gasstations_marked.txt and showed 'Gas station position saved' in every build; that is a developer tool now and only exists in the dev exe, so F7 is only the free camera key for players. Also corrected a comment in the shipped config.ini that named a file wrongly. Built the dev exe and ran the health check; the release exe

I added the cars of Destruction Derby (PlayStation). The Disc Install makes the game's one car body in six paints (Rookie, Amateur and Pro in the paints of player 1 and player 2) from your own disc, with the real door pictures, Driver 2 wheels and a car picture each. They show up as mods\Destruction Derby. Needs the disc. The roof, bonnet and window colours are plain colours, the 19 opponent paints are not found yet. Checked with the real disc and the car pictures on the second PC,

Added the 19 stock cars of Destruction Derby 2 (PlayStation). It is one NASCAR body with the paint and the door number of each driver, from The Master to Rivit, with their real names. They sit in the EXT tab. Disc Install makes them from your own disc (command line option --dd2 for now, no row in the window yet). The player cars Rookie, Amateur and Pro are not in yet.

Fixed the damage of a car zone overflowing: a very hard hit (a heavy chase runner, or two cars really colliding now that cars no longer ghost) added to a 16 bit number that wrapped negative, and the mirrored zone had no upper limit, so the dent picture of the car could read the wrong part of its texture page and show garbled noise. The damage is summed in a bigger number and kept between 0 and 4095. This is a likely cause of the garbled rear of a police car after a hit, but I could not reproduce that picture, so it is NOT confirmed.

Added the three player cars of Destruction Derby 2 (PlayStation): Rookie (white, red stripe), Amateur (white, purple stripe) and Pro (yellow, black stripe), on the same NASCAR body, with the 01 on the doors and a car picture each. They sit in the EXT tab next to the 19 drivers and come from the same Disc Install of your own disc. The colours match the wiki.

Fixed the Driv3r cars being the mirror image of the real cars: text, plates and decals (POLICE, SoBe, MIAMI, POLIS, number plates) read backwards and left and right were swapped. Checked in the game against the wiki pictures. Tried by the automatic tests only, The car files and the data lumps have to be made again.

Made the window glass of the Driv3r cars see through like the real game, so the seats, dash and steering wheel show inside. The glass picture kept its own alpha, before it was a dark solid slab. Tried by the automatic tests and pictures of 16 cars, The car files and the data lumps have to be made again.

Added all 16 body paints to the Driv3r cars (the customizer shows them as colour swatches, Paint 1 to 16). The game paints one white picture with a mask at load, so the cars stay at the same size on disk instead of 650 MB more.

Made the picture of the Driv3r cars sharper: every polygon now keeps its exact picture points in a new file next to the car picture (cars/tex/<id>.uv16), so lettering, rivets and lamps are no longer smeared into steps of 4 texels. Cars without the file look as before. Checked with pictures from a build on the second PC of a coupe, a bus and a taxi, The car files and the data lumps have to be made again (about 1.5 MB more).
Made the jobs and the CB radio stop picking their random numbers from the clock, so recorded runs play the same every time.
Changed pedestrians to be run over by traffic and police cars too, not only your own car. Only your own car gives you the hit and run felony.
Made pedestrians dodge cars less, and the dodge now counts for traffic and police cars too. Slow cars and your horn still make everybody get out of the way.
Slowed down how fast a hit pedestrian is thrown: a hit at 60 mph used to throw him about 12 metres, now about 2.7, and at 120 mph about 8. It counts for you, traffic and police cars alike.
Added Pedestrian Models (Automatic, Driver 2, Driv3r, Both) and Pedestrian Height to the Advanced People and Traffic page, saved with the other tweaks.
Fixed the names of the Chicago and Havana cars, for example the Buick GSX, the fire truck, the armored truck and the school bus.
Added a cockpit camera view: you sit on the left side of the car and see the bonnet with a dash that shows speed, rev counter and gear. (experimental, off by default, not finished)
Made the tail lamps of the converted Gran Turismo cars change from dim red to bright red with a glow when you brake, and the third brake lamp lights too. The cars must be made again by the setup.
Fixed Driver 1 tyres that hung low and small under their wheel arch (the Civilian 4 van, 4 more cars): they are bigger and fill the arch now, the ride height stays.

Changed the cockpit view: the steering wheel is one smooth ring now (no gaps), the dials are all analog (needles, no digits, a fuel dial and gear lamps) and sit higher so the wheel does not hide them, and each kind of vehicle gets its own simple inside: coupe, convertible (no roof), truck (bench seat), mini bus, bus (seat rows and an aisle) and the cop car with the cage between front and back. (experimental, off by default, not finished)

Lowered the dash in the cockpit view to a flat slab and made the dials smaller, so they sit low behind the top of the steering wheel and the windscreen with the bonnet fills most of the picture. The A pillars are thinner. (experimental, off by default, not finished)

Fitted the back of the cockpit cabin to the real car body: the roof ends where the body roof ends, the parcel shelf sits under the trunk lid, a short cabin or a long rear window slope gets a coupe cabin without a back bench, and the seats are smaller. Looking back now shows the real trunk and spoiler. (experimental, off by default, not finished)

Made the points on the car in the Lights and Exhaust tabs easy to read and to hit: a shape, a colour and a letter for every kind of light and for the pipe, an outline that shows on any paint, the name when the mouse is over a point, an orange halo with axes on the chosen one, a drag over the body of the car, the wheel over the chosen point resizes it, and a new light follows the mouse over the car until you click.

Added keyboard control to the Lights and Exhaust tabs: arrows and Page Up and Down nudge a point (Shift fine, Ctrl coarse), Tab chooses the next entry, M switches both sides, Del deletes, Ctrl+D copies, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo every change, and a number can be typed into every number row. The pipes got turn, tilt and style rows and a layout row. No pad controls were added.

Changed the exhaust pipes of every Gran Turismo 2 and Gran Turismo 1 car to sit where the car's own rear shows its pipes (single, dual, quad or none), from a by-eye table of all 1,417 cars. The old texture search matched the real pipes on only about one car in five. The cars must be made again by the setup.

Added a Smart Cop Difficulty option (Easy, Normal, Hard). Normal and Hard police aim ahead of you, ram instead of tailing, drive beside you and cut across open ground when they can see you; Hard also pits and blocks. Easy is the old Smart Cop.

Changed the Smart Cop on Normal and Hard so the police reach you much sooner: one or two more cars, replaced faster, and backups come out of side streets ahead of you instead of from far behind. They push you at your speed instead of hitting at full speed, and back out of a stuck spot sooner.

Added a repair pad to CatFlip's International Auto Exchange on Goose Island. Park on it, and you can pay to repair your car, pay for new plates that clear your felony, or sell the car (it only buys the cars it asks for, see the Pick List). Every player in a split screen has his own prices and his own wallet.
Added a shady CB call that asks for a car model: bring one to the Exchange for a better offer. Accepting costs nothing, there is no timer, and a player who does not answer loses nothing.

Fixed cars in traffic that could turn up with garbled, noisy textures after a long session (a bus with white and grey noise in Chicago): the pool that shares colour palettes between the Driver 1, Gran Turismo and pack cars stopped counting at 255 users and gave a palette back while cars still used it.

Changed the Auto Exchange to open as a menu when you press the action button on the pad. Up and down, Enter and Esc, the pad and the mouse all work, and the car no longer drives off when you press the arrows.

Changed the Auto Exchange to buy only the cars it asks for: the five cars of its new Pick List and the model the CB radio asks for. Any other car shows Not Needed, and a car over half damaged shows Too Damaged until you repair it. The damage lowers the price.

Added HOT: with a stolen car or a Pick List job the police are harder on you. They see you from 1.4 times as far, you cool off slower, backups come sooner and one more car chases you, and Smart Cops push harder. The heat panel reads HOT CAR.

Added speed traps to Take a Ride, eight radar spots on the main roads of each of the four cities. Pass one over 65 mph (105 km/h) and you get a SPEED TRAP message with your speed, a small fine from your wallet and a bump to your wanted level. The same trap waits a minute before it catches you again, and a stolen car gets a stricter limit.

Made jobs pay more at night (25 percent), in rain or on a wet road (15 percent) and 40 percent when both. Package runs, race wins, hits, shake-offs, protection rounds and tails say so in the job message. Taxi fares keep their own rates.

Reworked the Smart Cop chase. One cop on Normal and two on Hard now drive the road ahead of you to cut you off, the far cops follow the road route to you, and the cops hit less scenery and traffic (slower through traffic, cutting across only where the car fits, a cop ahead does not ram you head on). In a test with a computer driver the cops wreck less and stay near you more, and one chase in eight still ends in a getaway. It is not as hard as it should be yet.
Added a known problem to the README, some Havana and Rio cars have no model yet and cars newer than 1963 do not spawn in Havana

Added a radar post at every speed trap in Take a Ride: a pole with a camera box, a blinking lamp and a ring on the road, in the four Driver 2 cities and the four Driver 1 cities. When a trap catches you the screen flashes white, only in the view of the player who was caught. Fines and wanted level stay as they were.

Fixed the wheel positions of the Driver 1 van and pickup. The hubs now sit in the middle of their wheel openings and the tyres are sized to the arches. Checked on the side, front and rear pictures only.

Added tyre compounds to the customizer: the Wheels tab has a Tyre compound row, Normal (Driver 2), Race and Drift. Race grips, brakes and corners better but lets go faster past the limit. Drift lets the tail slide and holds the slide for you, the throttle sets the angle, lifting straightens, a throttle stab in a corner or the handbrake kicks the tail out with no clutch button. Drift Assist in the options (Off, Light, Full) sets how much the car steers into the slide. The tyre is saved with each car. Traffic, police and mission cars keep the normal tyres. Compounds are listed in cars/tyres.txt, modders can add their own. Race laps 3.6 percent faster, Drift holds 40 degrees for 8 seconds.

Reworked the Drift tyre. It no longer holds one angle for you: the slide now comes from weight transfer. Braking and lifting rotate the car, throttle gives power oversteer, a quick flick of the wheel swings the weight so you can throw the car from one slide into the other, and the car keeps its yaw momentum. Drift Assist (Off, Light, Full) is now only a gentle self-aligning help that gives way when you steer, plus a soft guard against spinning. Flick, S-bend and lift-off.

Made the Drift tyre easier and less snappy. The tail now lets go over a third of a second instead of at once, never drops below a safe grip, and tightens before a slide turns into a spin. A normal turn-in with the throttle starts a slide at 40 to 70 km/h, the clutch kick is softer and longer, and the steering help is stronger when the car is far sideways or turning fast but still gives way when you steer. A seeded sloppy driver holds a slide of 20 degrees or more for 3 seconds without a spin in 20 of 20 runs.

Rebuilt the Drift tyre as a real combined slip model: each axle has its own slip angle, the rear wheels have a slip ratio, and throttle takes lateral grip off the rear through a friction ellipse, so the slide comes from one tyre model. The wheel counts more at a big slip angle so the front can be thrown across fast, and a small drift-hold throttle trim (Drift Assist) helps keep a slide. Chains of six slides with no spin in 20 of 20 runs, 10 of 20 sloppy drivers hold a circle drift for 16 seconds or more.

Changed the handbrake on Drift tyres into a tool: the rear wheels no longer lock, a tap kicks the tail out like a clutch kick and keeps your speed, and holding it takes only a part of the rear grip. Smoothed the weight transfer, with lifting and re-applying the throttle shifting load front and back. Added a throttle blip kick: a quick stab from low to high throttle in a slide or turn-in dips the rear grip, spikes the revs and gives a short push, so you can tighten or re-throw a drift without a clutch pedal.

Fixed more Driver 2 car names with the IGCD list as the reference: Havana pickup is the Chevrolet Advance-Design 3100, Rio pickup is the Task Force 3100 (was Dodge C-Series), Vegas pickup is the Chevrolet K-10, Rio pickup is the Dodge Ram. Some Chicago cars and the Rio police car are still open, the IGCD list does not settle them.

Changed the Driver 2 car names to your picks: Chicago cars are the Oldsmobile 442 and the Oldsmobile Delta 88, the Havana police car is the De Soto Adventurer Police, the Rio police car is the GAZ 24 Volga Police.

sections.title: Cities and World
lines: Added maps with road and place names for Havana, Las Vegas and Rio.
Changed the city map pictures to be made on your own PC, so they no longer ship in the package. The Driver 1 cities build their own too, and Rio's street names no longer show on them.
Changed the map, place name and street name files, the city settings and the gas station list to be found by city id as well.
Added dawn, dusk and night as the time of day for Take A Ride, in all eight cities. A night ride uses the day level with the clock set to night.
Removed the automatic river mask, the generated water, the canal gap fill and the courtyard raster from the Driver 1 cities, the water pieces of the level editor replace them.
Fixed the road spikes in Los Angeles.
Changed Los Angeles to be a night city, so a ride there starts at night.
Fixed the game hanging in Los Angeles when it sampled the water.
Put the hand made water, canal and bridge pieces for Havana and Rio into the Core pack.
Fixed the Las Vegas night showing pedestrians and signal glows with scrambled colours after the day to night swap.
Fixed restarts keeping the old pedestrian ragdoll dice.
Fixed restarts keeping the old traffic counters, density limits and waiting cars.
Fixed the civilian lane change timing counting from the old level, it counts from the start of a level now.
Added 13 gas station lines for Las Vegas and Rio from the player survey.
Added 3 gas stations in Las Vegas found in the level data.
Fixed traffic cars picking a garbage distance along the road when they got confused while joining a road, this changed the San Francisco traffic.
Fixed the Chicago ferris wheel so it starts again after a restart, like a fresh start.
Replaced the Dumpster texture with a new one, same name, size and format.
Changed pedestrians to come in more looks, men and women with different clothes, and made them walk on sidewalks and crossings only.
Changed the game to build its own city level files from your discs (-buildlevels), so the installer no longer needs a separate tool for it, and the Core edits are baked into them.
Moved the sounds of a city (car banks, sirens, cop voices, ambient sounds, music, tunnels) into the city file, the defaults are the old values.
Moved the start positions, level folder and loading picture names, mission table and debris colours into the city file.
Changed the city file to say which handler runs the world, mission and object events, instead of a branch for each city in the code.
Moved the sky, sun, moon, light, police light and shadow values of a city into the city file, and the level builder writes them.
Changed level files to list every polygon, and patches can now hide a face by its number and move things.
Added patch format 4, which can retexture a face and add an object.
Changed high scores and replays to remember the city by name, old numbered scores and old replays still load, and a Driver 1 city in a replay becomes the active city.
Fixed Las Vegas giving different results from run to run, a road lookup was reading outside its data.
Changed travel to another city to work without restarting the game, the old city's assets are released. It is on by default now (the sceneLoad setting), and trips go through the scene loader.
Made the road lookup check its limits and stop in bad data, each case logs once.
Fixed a crash when starting a new game in a bigger city after another city, the old city's map store was read.
Fixed night start levels crashing story mission 30 and every city at the late hour, they now read the night from the level file.
Changed the night set of a package to come from the night level files, it was a second day level.
Changed the city list to hold up to 64 cities, the Take A Ride list, the Travel list and the missions now read it, and hidden levels can be left out of the lists.
Added listing and starting a city that is only a level file (a mod's own city), by trip and from the lists.

Added the Driver 1 credits level as a normal city called Newcastle, you pick it in Take A Ride and in the Travel list, the setup makes it with a loading picture. Cars drive there now, they start on the small road network because the level is smaller than the old traffic search.
Changed cities to load their roads and models from the city file, for day and night, and the disc is only a fallback (geometryFromLevel).
Fixed a trip carrying traffic and car paint of the old city into the new one.
Fixed Esc > Restart in the same city, the night after a restart no longer shows garbage textures and things a patch adds stay solid.
Changed a city that is only a level file to start at the start in its city.txt, and the Driver 1 levels the game makes carry the start the Driver 1 cities use.
Fixed buildings and colours missing in a new city after a trip back to Chicago.
Changed the Driver 1 cities to take their pedestrian animations from the Rio city file and removed the disc image directory walker.
Fixed jogging pedestrians with blotchy pants, clothes now change their colour at every brightness, only heads keep dark colours.

Moved the files of each Driver 2 city into its city file: Chicago, Havana, Vegas and Rio carry their car looks, car denting, loading picture and painted sky inside the .level, so they load from the city file alone. Other cities take the set of a Driver 2 level.
Fixed the sea showing under empty map cells near the tiles in the Driver 1 cities (Miami, San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York). Those cells are ground now. The setup has to convert the cities again.

Fixed knocked over lamp posts, signs and other smashables vanishing the moment they landed. They now land on the ground under them, topple flat (a lamp post lies with its arm on the sidewalk) and stay about a minute before they sink away, 64 at once, the oldest goes first. Checked by log numbers and pictures only,

Changed the traffic lights and parked cars so the traffic flows: two phase lights with a protected left turn (config.ini signalProgramme, 2 by default, 0 gives the old lights), at most 7 percent of the cars parked (parkedCarPercent), only one car in three tries to park, and a car that cannot park gives up. In a test run of 4 cities the cars pass the junctions about twice as often and far fewer cars stand for more than 30 seconds. With everything switched off the simulation is identical to before. Checked by automatic tests,

Gave a city of a mod its own high score tables: the four Driver 2 cities and the Driver 1 cities keep the tables of the original game, any other city gets a set found by its city name, saved in machine.sav under the city name (old saves load as before). Checked by automatic tests,

Made demos (file version 2), replays, the network room (protocol 3) and the edits file names of cities beyond the first eight use the city name instead of a number: old demos still play in their city, a demo or replay of a mod city plays in that city, a machine with another game version is told apart in the log, and an old edits_N.txt of such a city is copied (never moved) to edits_<city name>.txt with a .premigrate copy beside it. Checked by automatic tests,

Made a bake write the removals and moves of a patch into the level itself instead of keeping them as a patch layer that the game applies at every load. Every record is checked first, the hidden faces, pieces, retextures and added objects stay in the patch, the installed level is never written, RESET LEVEL and UNDO BAKE still work on the baked copy, and the switch bakeGeometry=0 keeps the old way. Checked by automatic tests,

Refused a damaged or incomplete level at load. The game checks the level file before it starts to use it (the parts lie inside the file, the textures, models, map and spool info are there). If something is wrong it writes the reason to the log, shows a message in your language and goes back to the menu instead of crashing. A texture, model or region that is damaged inside an otherwise good level no longer crashes or stops the game either. Tried with damaged copies of Chicago and Newcastle, the editor bake restart and five fuzz seeds,

Moved the places of the flyable helicopters and the airfield out of the code into a text file, aircraft/aircraft.txt of a pack. The Core pack ships the Chicago rows, so the spawns are the same as before; a mod can add rows for its own city, a damaged line is skipped and counted, a pack without the file adds nothing. It is described in the modding file list (section 17). Checked by automatic tests,

Made the car sets of a city data driven. The set a city drives and what the car picker calls each car (street or special) are now the keys cars.set and cars.kinds of its city.txt, and the car pool, the swaps for the night, the car extras and the sound and effect keys work for up to eight sets of car files (the four Driver 2 cities, and sets 4 to 7 that a mod can bring) instead of four fixed rows. The eight cities play as before. A set of a mod with real car files is Checked by automatic tests, nothing tried by hand.

A replay, a demo or a mission that is made in a city you do not have is now refused with a line in the log instead of playing in the wrong city. The mission maker now writes the city id next to a mission made in a city beyond the four Driver 2 cities. Old replays, demos, saves and missions load as before and the eight first cities are still written the old way. Checked with tests and damaged files only,

Fixed the pause Travel page: it held only 64 rows, a full city list has up to 72. Cities beyond the 64 the list can hold are now named in the log. Tried with a scratch game folder of 70 empty city files: 64 cities listed, a trip into an empty one is refused and goes back to the menu. The Take A Ride panel and the Travel page on screen with that many rows.
Fixed the far view carrying its ring size and a collision dummy model of the old city into the next one after a city change. Checked by automatic tests,

Added country rules to the traffic. The American cities get mostly American cars, Rio and Newcastle get cars of their own country, and Havana never gets a car newer than 1963. The rules are text files in the Core pack, one per city. The traffic of every city now draws other cars than before.

Goose Island is now CatFlip's International Auto Exchange: the two big halls by the south road got a REPAIR sign and a SHOWROOM sign, the apron east of them got painted parking stalls for 36 cars and light poles, a big CatFlip billboard stands by the road, and the map has the new names. The list of places (repair spot, showroom door, parking stalls) is in, so the repair pad and the showroom door work there. Checked by automatic tests and pictures,

Added hidden packages to Take a Ride. About 40 lie around each of the four Driver 2 cities. Drive or walk up to one and it is yours: a small cash reward, and a message that says how many you found. Every player counts his own, a package taken is gone for everybody until the level loads again. The Stats page shows your total and how many you found in this city. Checked by automatic tests only;

Fixed Traffic By Time Of Day also thinning the traffic inside missions: a mission now keeps its full traffic at any hour (the night curve made the escape template mission end in failure). Checked by automatic tests,

Lit the new light poles on Goose Island: they now light the ground at dusk and night like the city street lamps, and the lamp heads are warm instead of pale blue. Both halls of CatFlip's International Auto Exchange got ceiling lights, a spot over the repair pad and the display stall, and a light at each east opening, so the insides and the apron glow at night. Light markers now fade in with the same dusk curve as the street lamps. A light pole from the editor objects list brings its light along. Looked at test pictures at 19:30, 21:00 and 23:00. The floor inside the halls is still black.

Added the parked cars on the car lot of CatFlip's International Auto Exchange on Goose Island. When you come within about 25000 units, 24 to 34 of the 36 stalls fill with cars, every game day with another mix, at most 12 different models (only cars the game already has loaded, no new loading), and one show car stands in the showroom hall. They stand with the handbrake on and move when you hit them, and they go away when you leave. A car you drive off is stolen and the stall is filled again after 3 real minutes with another model. In split screen the lot stays full when only player 2 is near. Checked by automatic tests and pictures,

Changed the car lot: a taken stall is filled again after 3 real minutes whatever the day length, and the lot cars are no longer removed by the traffic's distance rule, so a lot that only the second player stands near stays full. The shop checks a lot car first (we know that car), then Not Needed, then Too Damaged. Checked by the log tests,

Gave the repair shop and the showroom on Goose Island a light concrete floor, so the insides are no longer pitch black at night. The repair pad stays open in the floor so its marker still shows. Only test scene pictures at 23:00.

Added a key over the showroom door pad and a wrench over the repair pad of the Auto Exchange, so each pad shows what it is. They grow in from a distance and vanish close up so the camera never looks into them.

Moved a third of the hidden packages of every city from the road to the sidewalk and into alleys beside the road (still within 10 m of a road, so a car or a walker gets there), and made package files for the four Driver 1 cities, 30 spots each. The packages and the Packages row of the stats page work there like in the Driver 2 cities; they stay off in the Driver 1 missions. Checked by automatic tests,
Updated the Core pack level edits and added two textures, concrete light and ramp asphalt, from the maker's editor work.

Changed the Driv3r Miami ground: the flat colour plane no longer lies over the lawn, paving, plaza and park models of the disc, streets get a real asphalt picture, near ground quads are 2 m, long road, wall and hedge textures no longer smear. Looked at pictures from 4 spots on the dev PC, no second PC run.

Changed the bonus cities ground: Ashland and London do not draw the flat ground file any more (grey wedges gone along the Ashland highway), Miami gets a sand strip where the land meets the sea. Pictures of 4 Miami spots, 3 Ashland spots and 1 London street on the dev PC.

Made Ashland's own cars appear in Ashland. The setup now writes the Police, AIPolice and CopJeep cars as cruisers, the BMW, Cadillac, Lincoln, Limo, PizzaCar, Viper, vans and the Taxi as street cars of Ashland only (before, all 17 were special and the traffic never picked them). Ambulance, Bus, Tank and APC stay special. On a second PC with the disc made cars, 2 of 2 new logchecks pass: about two thirds of the traffic picks are Ashland cars, the cruisers are the Ashland police cars.

Fixed the bonus cities Ashland and Miami showing as a mirror image (the Fender sign read backwards): the city, ground, roads, start and collision now share one frame (mirrorZ 0). London was checked on its shop signs and stays as it is. Checked by pictures from the game with a free camera;

Changed the chase camera to ignore invisible collision boxes and boxes buried under the road, so it does not jump close in front of an empty street. The strange camera of the player report was not reproduced.

Fixed Driver 2 pedestrians getting blue and violet hands and necks. The skin colours of a pedestrian palette are now found by comparing the palettes of the disc, so dark and strong skin shades stay skin and only the clothes change colour. Looked at in a 150 pedestrian crowd by day.

Turned the road heights of the bonus cities to the right sign: on hills the roads of Ashland (and London, Miami) lay upside down against the ground, the road files are fixed when loaded, no new city file needed. Only checked by tests and a sweep of 21777 road points,
Cars that fell through the ground of Ashland and kept falling are taken out now (a civilian car 7 m under the ground). The cause, lanes of the road file that run into a cliff, is not fixed.

Fixed cars falling through bridge decks over a valley in the bonus cities: where a road map cell holds two layers the road writer listed them in the wrong order, so the wheels always read the lowest one. Ashland, Miami and London need the setup to make their packages again. The checks (Ashland, Miami, London drive) pass,

Added a mesh cutter to the Italian Job car converter, so a film car that is over the car store limits is cut down to fit and a car with only one model (Jeep, Armoured Car) gets its lod1 and lod2 made. Added lamp positions, a driving class (the nearest Driver 2 body type) and a police siren with engine sounds for the film cars. Tested on made up meshes only,
Changed the ground of London under the blocks from one flat grey to a few tones: three block greys, a lighter road and a darker kerb and pavement. Tested on a made up world only,

Gave each Driver 1 city its own pair of songs (Frisco and New York from Chicago and Vegas, Los Angeles from Vegas, Miami from Havana) so they no longer all play Rio's. The disc has no Driver 1 music files. Script tested only,

Filled the notch of open sea at every convex corner of the shore in the Driv3r Miami bonus city: the sand strip along a diagonal shore stopped at each step and left a square gap. The shore line itself is still the 2 m ground raster (the GWTR chunk of the disc holds the sea tile placements, not shore lines). Pictures from the second PC only,

Fixed fences, walls, hedges, houses and street lamps of the Driv3r Miami bonus city standing turned the wrong way (up to 90 degrees) so fence pieces did not connect: the setup turned every placed object with the transposed matrix, and it read the 5184 placements that hold a quaternion as a plain yaw. Now 64 percent of the fence ends meet, before 29 percent, and the collision boxes turn with the objects. Objects that lean on a slope still stand upright. Checked with a new fence connection test and pictures from the disc data, a new package was made in a scratch folder.

I made London from The Italian Job the right size next to a Driver 2 car. The film game is built at about three quarters of real size (its Mini is 2.28 units for a 3.05 m car), so streets, kerbs, doors and lamp posts were too small. The map and the converted film cars now use one scale of 4/3 m per game unit (Mini 3.04 m, Miura 4.41 m). Checked with the converter, tests and pictures,

I fixed mess in the London buildings: the closed back walls and roofs I add to the facades made slanted ribbons that showed through the windows, some faces were turned the wrong way and the roofs had thin spikes. Now there is one depth per building and the faces and normals agree. Roofs of odd shaped buildings are still rough. Checked with the new geometry audit and pictures,

Fixed the broken geometry of Ashland. The mission versions of the city pieces were drawn on top of the normal ones (25451 triangles on top of each other, speckled walls and wrong shapes); now only the normal city is made, the ground and collision no longer use the mission pieces, the invisible collision hulls are not drawn and the triangle winding is the same as in London. Ashland has to be made again by the setup.

Fixed the mirrored Driv3r Miami: every text and sign read backwards (the NVIDIA wall sign) because the whole city was drawn as a mirror image. The package now says mirrorZ 1, roads, ground, collision and the start follow. Checked in the game on the NVIDIA sign,

Fixed the towers of Driv3r Miami that lost their walls: a facade picture with only two alpha values (windows 255, wall bands 17) was cut out by the alpha test, so only the window quads were left floating.

Fixed the level of detail of Driv3r Miami models: the seven mesh slots of a model are not a chain from fine to coarse (slot 1 of a tower is a flat disc, slots 2 and 3 hang under the ground, slot 4 is glass only). Only a slot that is the model again with fewer triangles is a LOD now; the package got 17 MB smaller.
Fixed the rectangular gaps in the ground of Driv3r Miami: a hole in the ground file that touches a tile edge was taken for the sea. A hole under roofs is a city block and gets ground now.

Changed the Driv3r Miami streaming: every object picks its level of detail by the size it has on the screen and a tile is baked again when a visible pick changes (before, whole 480 m tiles switched at once). Visible pops on a 4.3 km flight at 85 m: 2338 to 864 per km, costs 21 percent more triangles. Added the pop meter REDRIVER_BIGCITYFLY (radius speed height laps).

Fixed the blue and grey spikes along the edges of ground patches in the roads of Driv3r Miami: the cover test now looks at quarter metre squares, so a quad on a slanted kerb is no longer skipped when a corner of it is not covered. Checked on pictures,

Fixed the tan fins and grey sheets hanging in the canal water along the quay walls and under the monorail in Driv3r Miami: sand skirts only grow on low beach shores now, and ground at a quay, pier or deck edge is left to the models. Checked on pictures,

Made the Driv3r Miami beach one sand beach that slopes into the water: the ground gets the sand picture and the flat 200 metre sand sheets of the disc, which floated over the sea as pale rectangles, are left out. Needs the Miami package made again by the setup. Checked on pictures,

Fixed the dark grey rectangles in the streets of Driv3r's Miami: the ground fill under the roads is now the same light tone as the street models, and a thin sheet under the models closes hairline gaps to the sea. The lane strips the disc builds from its road data are still missing, so the fill has no wear marks or lane lines

Laid the street picture along the Miami road graph, so the grey rectangles in the lanes and the median are filled with lanes with wear and the yellow centre line. The disc has no placed piece for them: the JNR! chunk is only the collision quad tree, no road data.

Fixed the blue grey line across the Miami road and the shadows that did not match: the hidden stand in level threw its own shadows onto the city. The Miami buildings, palms and lamps now cast the sun shadows themselves.

Fixed the Driv3r Miami cars growing two 3 m long light cones in front after the triangle count fix. The cone parts are left out again, and the racer and sports coupe 2 lose the cones they always had (their length goes from 7.3 and 7.8 m to 4.6 and 4.9 m). Checked on 15 cars with triangle counts and pictures and a unit test;

Closed the gap in the lift bridge of the Miami bonus city: the middle span is not in the disc data, so the converter now finds the hole by its shape (two deck ends facing each other over water) and lays a deck of the street picture across it. Looked at in pictures on the second PC,

Removed the pale grey slabs that floated in the Miami canals: they were flat pieces of the sea bed that showed through the water at a low angle, the city layer no longer draws flat triangles under the sea level. A faint reflection of the quay stays in the water. Looked at in pictures,

I filled the missing walkway of the Miami lift bridge. The span between the two leaves only got a road lane before, so both pavements and both kerb strips stopped at the leaf ends and left an 18 m hole. Now the span gets pavement, kerb and road across the whole width, each with its own picture, and the walkable ground over the span is as wide as the picture. I also fixed a bug where a fresh setup made no span deck at all. Checked with pictures from above, from walking height and at car height, and with the unit tests. Nobody walked or drove over it. The railing along the span is still open: the disc has no model for it.

I fixed the player on foot in the bonus cities (Driv3r Miami, London, Ashland). Their empty level has none of Tanner's body parts, so he came out as a white block figure. Now Tanner of Driv3r is drawn there when the setup made him; the civilian stand in at the same place stays out so there is one figure. Chicago and the Driver 1 cities are unchanged. I looked at the picture of the Miami on foot scene before and after (white blocks before, a man in a dark shirt after) and at the Chicago on foot picture (same as before).

I made the nights in Ashland and London brighter (night gain 0.55 to 0.8): the cliff wall and skyline now come out of the dark and the headlights are still the brightest thing. You picked the value from pictures. Ashland still has no lit street lamps at its lamp posts, that is not fixed.

Gave the bonus cities (London, Miami, Ashland) the wheel models and wheel pictures of Chicago, made from your own disc by the setup, so cars have round wheels there. Checked by hand in the London customizer: the wheels look good. Packages made before have to be made again, or run through the new rdcontent level rewheel.

Fixed the smeared roofs in London: the roof texture numbers were too big for the package and every vertex of 200 buildings was clamped. The London package has to be made again to get it. The glass atrium at the top left still looks odd.

Put stand-in cars into the Havana and Rio traffic for the cars that still have no model. Havana: the Wolseley 6/99 for the Peugeot 404 and the Fiat 600 for the Renault 4 (both from the Italian Job pack, so only when you made that pack), and the Driver 1 Thunderbird takes the share of the six 1950s American cars that are still missing. Rio: the VW Beetle for the Fusca, the Chevrolet Nova for the Opala, the Ford Granada for the Maverick and the Dodge Charger for the Polara. Fixed the Driver 1 Thunderbird, which could not spawn in Havana any more since the Driver 1 cars got their real names. Only the tick hash (31 Havana and Rio scenarios move, on purpose), the traffic log and one picture of each car in its city.

Removed the massive test ramp at the Chicago gas station. Both ramps (two wedges, 3400 long, 650 high) are gone from the Core level edits and the road is flat again. Checked with a picture from above before and after, and the level builds and verifies.

I added circuits and sprints for the online race events in Chicago (2 more), Havana, Las Vegas and Rio (2 more each). They sit in a new file maps/raceevents_<city>.txt that the game reads in an online room only, so single player Take a Ride keeps its old courses. A test checks that every point is on a street, every leg is joined by streets and the start grid is on the road.

Added the Driv3r motorcycles, the go-kart, the boats, the Istanbul tram and train and the trailers as models, made by the setup from your own Driv3r PC disc into the Driv3r Miami pack (models folder, plain OBJ files with their pictures that the level editor can place). Models only: they do not drive, float or run on rails yet, and they are not in the car picker. The Miami monorail is not found yet. Tried by the unit test and a disc install into a scratch folder only,

Added the Driv3r cars of Nice and Istanbul: 20 cars of Nice and 14 of Istanbul, with their real in-game names (Le Chariot Cinq, Dagger Type-T, Otobus, '54 Taxi and so on), the police cars of both cities, taxis, buses and vans. The Disc Install makes them from your own Driv3r PC disc next to the Miami cars, and they show in the EXT tab with a picture each. They have no city of their own yet, so they only show in the car picker and the garage. Tried by unit tests, a disc run in a scratch folder and pictures, The rear wheels of several of them still stand out of the body (wheel work is separate).
Changed traffic so it appears and disappears farther away the faster you drive in a sheet car. The sheet physics is off by default and still being tuned.
Fixed black and white noise on big Chicago walls at night with the Driver2 texture fixes mod on.

Locked the show car in the Auto Exchange showroom: you cannot get in, it takes no damage and it goes back to its place when something pushes it. The cars on the lot are still for sale and for stealing.

Fixed the Miami models losing the last triangle of every strip: the wedge shaped holes in the quay walls, the broken canal walls and the missing bridge deck pieces came from one wrong count in the model reader. One triangle models are kept now too. Made by the setup from your Driv3r disc,
Changed the Miami beach: the sand models of the disc that floated over the sea as pale fingers are no longer drawn, the ground draws the sand, and the sand gets darker towards the water.

sections.title: Driver 1 and Gran Turismo
lines: Fixed Gran Turismo car decals under a bigger panel (like taillights set back in the boot lid), they are drawn in front of it now.
Changed the Yellow Cab to ship only the repainted pixels as an overlay over the picture from your own disc.
Fixed oversized wheels on the Driver 1 cars in traffic, and mods no longer replace the Driver 1 cars of a converted city.
Fixed a crash when getting out of the car in a Driver 1 city.
Changed Tanner to show up in the Driver 1 cities, the setup now adds his 16 models and his texture page to every city.
Put the Driver 2 cars of Rio back in the Driver 1 traffic, with their own bodies and textures.
Changed the setup to fit the Driver 1 PlayStation cars to Driver 2 sizes: cruisers per axis, long cars shortened, collision box from the real width.
Gave the 30 Driver 1 PC cars the same size fit as the PlayStation cars.

Added a tool that turns every car of a Gran Turismo 1 disc into a performance sheet (power, gears, tyres, drive type). The sheets are off by default and the physics that uses them is still being tuned.
