Added Find discs in a folder to the disc page of the installer. Point it at one folder and it searches that folder and its sub folders for every disc image it knows and fills in the rows, with a progress window, a Cancel button and a summary of what is still missing.
Fixed the Driver 1 PC row of the setup, which took the Windows disc of Driv3r for the Driver 1 PC disc.

Removed the old setup that was run inside the unzipped game folder. The game comes as one installer file now, and running the installer again on the same folder adds a disc or repairs the game. uninstall.exe in the game folder only uninstalls.

Rebuilt the installer window after the new launcher mockup: the installer picture is the whole window, a white bar at the bottom with a plain gear icon (options), the progress with one status line, and red pill buttons. The window shows one card, Add your game discs: license, folder, the two Driver 2 discs, the extras with their disc rows, and the folder search, all in one place; INSTALL is on once the license is ticked and the discs are in order. Progress, Cancel as a small link, and the result with PLAY, OPEN FOLDER and VIEW LOG pills are on that same window. The gear holds language, folder, shortcuts and the disc report. No page by page wizard any more. Every installer step, disc check and switch is as before. 4 new texts in 20 languages. Layout test (21 languages x 4 scales), the disc scan test and the window smoke with real Driver 2 discs (install and cancel) pass.

Made the game folder tidier: only the launcher and the uninstaller sit in the main folder, the game, the Car Creator and their DLLs are in a bin folder. The game finds its folder from there by itself, the installer, the shortcuts, the launcher and the Car Creator know the new place, and a folder of an older install is tidied when you install over it. Only the automatic tests ran (unit tests, a start of the game from bin, the release scan).

Changed the installer's progress line to Part 3 of 12 - name of the part, and the license text now says to close the setup if you do not accept (the second choice is gone, it is one tick). 2 new texts in 20 languages. Layout test (21 languages x 4 scales) passes.

Fixed the INSTALL button of the launcher, which did nothing. It now installs the whole game over the update channel. When no update is published yet (today the server has none) the status line says so: No update is published yet. Use Disc Install, or try again later. The button says INSTALL whenever the game is missing, also when an update was found. Layout checked by the automatic test in all 21 languages,

Added Disc Install to the launcher: a small link next to the bar while the game is missing and a button in Options. The launcher fetches the disc installer from the update server, checks the signed list and the hash of the file, and only then starts it on the game folder. It asks for all your discs and converts everything on your PC; nothing made from a disc is downloaded or uploaded. The setup got a --discs-only mode for this (no game files, no shortcuts, no uninstaller). 8 new texts in 21 languages (machine translation, native review owed). Tested by unit tests with a stub installer and by a tree compare with the Driver 2 discs (201 files equal),

Changed the last page of Disc Install: the button now says Open the launcher and starts the launcher from the game folder, then the setup closes. If the launcher is not there, the button is off and the text says so. The normal installer still starts the game.

Changed INSTALL in the launcher to be the only way to install. First it gets the program files from the update server, then the game data: a tester account gets the data from the server, everyone else gets Disc Install from their own discs. Removed the Disc Install button and the Tester access and Game lump buttons from Options, and the Disc Install link on the status line. The real server and the setup with a real data lump were not tried.
I fixed the update server so it hands out the Disc Install program; before, the launcher got a 404 when it asked for it. Tested with the server unit test; the live server still needs the update.

Added a first step to the Disc Install wizard: it says you must own the original discs, that the mod has no game data in it and that your files stay on your PC, shows the license and the credits, and Next stays grey until you tick I own these discs and agree. The tick is remembered for that game folder, so adding a disc later does not ask again. Checked by unit tests, a window test with no disc and the layout test in 21 languages at 100, 125, 150 and 200 percent.

Split the last disc row of the wizard into three: Driv3r, The Italian Job (PC) and World's Scariest Police Chases each get their own tick, path box, Browse and disc name, and a disc in the wrong row is refused with a hint. Find discs in a folder fills each row. The conversion itself is unchanged. Checked by the disc scan unit test and the layout test.

I built Disc Install into the launcher. After INSTALL the license, your disc rows (all nine, with Find discs in a folder) and the progress open inside the launcher window, and the launcher no longer downloads a separate installer to convert your discs. The convert code runs hidden inside the launcher's own files and reports its steps to the window. Tested by the automatic checks (the pages in 21 languages at four sizes, a fake engine, the real engine without discs).

Made game update releases possible as ONE lump file with the extension .update, in the same container as the data lumps: a full one for a fresh install or Repair and a small one with only the changed files and a list of removed files for the next build. The launcher picks a chain of the small ones when that is less to download, checks every file inside, and keeps the signature, the rollback, the self update and the player files exactly as before. Publish and upload tools and the server route are in, tested on loopback with a fake package only; nothing is deployed, and the launcher window was

Fixed the texts that still sent you to reDriver_Setup.exe: the modding guides, the Linux steps, the install readme and the two messages the game shows when game data files are missing now say to run the installer again, and the readme names Disc Install in the launcher. The two messages are translated into all 21 languages (machine quality).

I changed the last texts that still sent you to the old setup. The level editor message about a missing level file and the console message about missing Driv3r characters now say to open the launcher and choose Disc Install (Serbian and Ukrainian lines updated, the other languages show the English line). I also removed one unused text of the installer. Checked by the language and installer text tools only; I have not tried it by hand.

I made the launcher take over a game folder that was installed with the old installer (0.4.0-beta of 13 November). The update checks every file by hash and downloads only what differs. Then the old programs in the root move to updates\adopted, the shortcuts and the Apps entry follow the launcher, and uninstall.exe is replaced by the one of the new layout. Saves, settings, mods and game data are not touched. Tested with a copy of a real old install and a local test server: not tried by hand, not tried on the real server.

I fixed an update that stopped and rolled back when two files of the release had the same bytes (the same texture in two packs): the first one took the downloaded copy and the second found none. Found with the old install test.
I fixed the downloaded update file staying in updates\staging after an update (it kept its own file open, a full release is far over 100 MB).

I moved the license to its own first step in the disc install wizard: the license page comes first (I own these discs and agree, then Next), and the disc list page no longer shows the license box or a second tick. The tick is still remembered per game folder in the launcher window, Start on the first screen still needs it. Tested with the layout test (21 languages, 4 scales) and a window test of the page order;

Changed the installer and launcher texts that said run the setup again: they now say open the launcher and press Disc Install, in 13 installer window texts plus the launcher, 20 languages. The same for the damaged / missing level file messages, the editor help and the credits lines. The admin hint says start the launcher as administrator. Checked by the language and unit tests only, How the lines look in the installer window and the launcher, and the translations are machine made.

Changed the README, the editor manual, the modding guides, THIRD_PARTY files and the config comments to say Disc Install or the installer where they said the setup. The Online sentence in the README Known problems is its own bullet now and says what is true: early test code, greyed out until I switch it on, not tried by hand and not on two real home networks, no matchmaking.

Fixed the error at the end of a Disc Install that said setup_log.txt was used by another program. The install itself was fine; only the log copy in setup_report.txt was empty. Checked by the launcher unit tests,

Fixed a fresh install from the launcher having an empty config folder, so the game opened small (800x600) with no settings. The launcher now puts the shipped settings and name lists there when they are missing and never replaces your own changed files. Checked by the launcher unit tests (15 of 15),

Moves the nine core folders (Core pack, Ashland, London, Driver 1 Missions, car photos, Goose Island and the Driv3r characters) out of the mods folder in the engine: the game now reads them as built-in packs from GAME_DATA/PACKS, always on, the Core first, before the real mods. An old install that still has them in mods keeps working (that copy is used until PACKS has the pack, never both), and the level edits of the old Core folder are copied over once without overwriting. The level editor saves into the new place, the mods screen and the mod check show them as built-in and still report a mod that changes a file of one. Mod fingerprint and batch cache hash do not depend on where a pack lives. Tick hash identical in both layouts (same 166 ok, same 18 that already differed before).

Moved the game's own packs out of the mods folder into GAME_DATA/PACKS: Ashland, The Italian Job London, Driver 1 Missions, car photos, Goose Island, Driv3r characters and the Core pack are part of the game, not mods. Mods keeps BetterCars, Driver2TextureFixes and your own mods. The package stages them there, Disc Install makes Ashland, London and the Driver 1 missions there, and an older install is moved over once with the level edits and the disc built data (the setup log says what was moved, nothing is overwritten). An old data lump still installs into the new place. Checked by the setup lump tests and the rdbuild self test,

Changed the updater for the packs in GAME_DATA/PACKS: the packs made from your discs stay untouched, level edit files and engine sounds are kept, the shipped packs are replaced like other game files. When an update moves a shipped pack out of mods, the old copy is taken away into the rollback folder when you did not change it, a changed copy is left and written to the launcher log. Checked by the launcher unit tests (15 of 15),

Cleaned up and regrouped the shipped config.ini by topic (setup, draw distance, traffic, cars, light and weather, sound, online, controls). Removed the dead userChases line. Every setting keeps its value. The release config check passes.

Added a Disc Install step that turns the nine CD audio tracks of the Driver 1 PC disc into WAV files in GAME_DATA/SOUND/DRIVER1. It reads the German, Spanish, USA, French and Italian dumps and the English Nero image, and skips a disc without audio (the PlayStation images have none). Tested on scratch copies by the tools only,
Changed the made-by line of THIRD_PARTY.txt (water texture, main menu picture, installer picture) to say CatFlip instead of me. Text only.

Reworded the credits in THIRD_PARTY.txt and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: the weather and aircraft sounds belong to CatFlip, one trademark sentence for Driver, Driver 2, Driv3r and Gran Turismo, and the made-by lines say CatFlip. Text only.

Changed the launcher update so the one update file is unpacked while it downloads. A thread reads the end of the file first, cuts every file out as soon as its bytes are there and builds the check hash on the way, so there is no wait for 3000+ files after the download. On a scratch test with 3121 files the unpack after the download went from 11.7 s to under 0.1 s. The hash check of the whole file and every file stays, a broken transfer falls back to the old way.

Changed the launcher progress bars. Every step has its own real percent and stops at 99 until the step is done, steps with no total (checking, making the city files, disc steps without a percent) show a moving bar with the step name, the unpack and the check of a download have their own text, and the Disc Install bar counts steps and never goes back. After an update with no discs in the install the launcher asks once to run Disc Install again so the city files match online games.

Changed INSTALL in the launcher into one flow with one bar. It lists every step (check, download the program files, install them, your discs, download the game data, install it, check the files, city files) with the done ones ticked, and the line under the bar says Step 3 of 9 and the name. The percent is weighted by the real work (download sizes, unpack, the disc conversion), never goes back and says waiting for you where you have to act. Only the layout pictures, the unit tests and a small local install ran.

Fixed the launcher stopping in the middle of INSTALL after it updated itself. The new launcher now goes on with INSTALL by itself (game data, discs, city files) and does not need to be closed and opened again. A local install with a self update ran, not the real list.

Fixed the launcher saying Play after INSTALL and Update after the next start. The game data and the discs rewrite some files of the update list, so INSTALL now ends with the list run once more from the file that is still there (no second download) and the button shows what a fresh start would show. The unit test does the same steps on a scratch folder.

Moved BetterCars, Driver2TextureFixes and Driv3r Miami out of the mods folder in the engine: they are built-in packs of GAME_DATA/PACKS now, always on, and load in the same order as before (after the Core pack and the other game packs, before your mods). A Driv3r Miami that Disc Install made in mods is moved to GAME_DATA/PACKS once at the next start (one rename, nothing is copied). An old mods copy of BetterCars or Driver2TextureFixes is used until the update has put the pack in place. The content check of online rooms did not change. Checked on a copy of a 1302 install: the same pack order, the same identity file, with the old layout and with the new one.

Changed Disc Install and the data lumps for the three new core packs: the Driv3r Miami city and its cars are made in GAME_DATA/PACKS/Driv3r Miami, and the setup moves an older mods/Driv3r Miami, mods/BetterCars and mods/Driver2TextureFixes there once (nothing is overwritten). An old data lump with mods/Driv3r Miami paths is installed in the new place. Unit test lump passes.

Changed the package and the update for BetterCars and Driver2TextureFixes: they ship in GAME_DATA/PACKS, and the update takes the old copies in mods away (into the rollback folder, only when you did not change them). A file of your own in mods/BetterCars stays where it is. The Driv3r Miami folder made from your disc is never in an update list. Checked by the launcher unit tests (launcher_core, launcher_update).

Updated the Known problems of the README: removed dynamic weather, restarting a mission, Driver 1 cars and cities and the editor, and rewrote the Online line (Online is open, two real PCs joined a room on my server). Text only.
Removed split screen from the Known problems of the README: the smaller shadow and reflection maps and closer fog per view are by design. Text only.

Made the launcher INSTALL download the game data for everybody in the testing phase. No tester account and no discs needed. It takes the data from a signed public list, checks every file and installs it like the tester path. Without that list it asks for the discs as before. Disc Install is still there: tick it in Options.

Put the experimental Destruction Derby cars into the game data download: they travel in the same part as the Driv3r cars, so a download install has them without the discs. Checked by the lump unit test,

Fixed the realistic car physics file not reaching players through the update: config/carsheet.ini was left out as a settings file. It is now a seed file of the update, written when missing and kept when the player changes it. Checked with the launcher unit tests, and a test install showed the file missing before the fix.

Fixed the hidden INSTALL click of the launcher (--auto-install, used by tests and scripts) stopping at the Your own discs page when the public game data list is on the server. It now takes the same way as the INSTALL button in the window for a player who is no tester: it finds the public list, downloads the base, update and disc installer data, installs it and ends with the same result lines. With no list it still ends at the Disc Install page. Auto tested,

sections.title: Translations
lines: Translated the level editor manual into all languages.
Translated the level editor button tooltips into all languages and made the tooltip box fit longer texts.
Translated the new setup texts for the Gran Turismo discs, archives and Driver 1 cities into all languages.
Translated the city maps step of the setup and its messages into all languages.
Translated the Traffic Cars and Extended Cars texts into all languages.
Added a language report to the translation tool, it lists the missing and the wrong lines for all languages.
Added a pseudo language to the translation tool, it helps to find text that does not fit or is not translated.
Added two translation tool commands that find text in the code that is not yet in the translation sheets and wrap tables so they can be translated.
Added the English texts for the pause menu Players submenu (1 to 8 players), and gave the Start Game row of the Multiplayer menu its own text in all languages.
Added about 240 new texts in all languages (game modes, Multiplayer menu, profiles, local players, credits), machine translated.
Translated 117 new texts (CB package, Courier, Multiplayer Local and Online, car picker, profile manage) into Czech, Slovak and Polish, machine translated.
Translated the same 117 new texts into French, Italian, Spanish and Romanian, machine translated.
Translated the same 117 new texts into German, Hungarian, Turkish, Greek and Russian, machine translated.
Added the new editor texts in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Romanian, Czech, Slovak, Polish, Russian, Greek, Hungarian and Turkish (round 4, machine translated, no native review yet).
Fixed the editor label NEW to use the feminine form (scene and mission) in French, Italian, Romanian and Greek.
Translated the 423 new editor texts into German, French, Spanish and Italian (round 5, machine translated).
Translated the 423 new editor texts into Czech, Slovak, Polish, Hungarian and Romanian (round 5, machine translated).
Translated the 423 new editor texts into Russian, Greek and Turkish (round 5, machine translated).
Added the SAVE FAILED message of the level editor in all languages.
Added the 28 new installer texts in all languages (machine translated) and fixed the uninstaller leaving a file behind.
Translated the BAKE, RESET LEVEL and no surface messages of the editor into all languages.
Translated the file browser texts and the remaining editor help texts into all languages.
Added the 62 new editor texts in all languages (machine translated, no native review).
Filled the missing texts in Czech (215 texts), Slovak and Polish (machine translated, no native review).
Filled the missing texts in Hungarian, Romanian and Greek (machine translated, no native review).
Filled the missing texts in French, German and Italian, with the CB radio names and the weather and headlights options.
Filled the missing texts in Spanish, Russian and Turkish, with the CB radio names and the weather and headlights options.
Repaired broken characters in the Russian, Greek, Polish and Spanish editor texts.
Added five missing texts in six languages and shortened five over-long lines.

Added Brazilian Portuguese as a language: the HUD, jobs, CB radio, game texts, missions, credits, the main menu, pause menu and options, the subtitles, the game modes and the taxi texts (shortened the taxi fare multiplier label). Machine translated, a native speaker review is still to come.
Translated the level editor into Brazilian Portuguese.

Translated the texts of the new level editor look into all languages (machine translated, not checked by a native speaker). 150 texts per language. Looked at pictures of the editor in German, Russian, French, Greek, Hungarian, Turkish and Polish.
Translated the new setup step Shared disc data into the 12 setup languages, plus five older setup messages that were still English. Machine translated, not checked by a native speaker.
Translated the new editor help pages and the tool palette words into the other 13 language folders, plus the out-of-memory message box. Machine translated, no native review.

Translated the new menu texts into all languages: the Blood row, Local Players, Keyboard 3 and 4, Gamepad 5 to 8, the car group options, Pedestrians Crossing Roads and two titles of the mods menu. Machine translated, no native review.

Translated the new options texts (page and group names, the new settings, one line of help per row) into all languages: Czech, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Slovak, Spanish and Turkish. Machine translation, not reviewed by a native speaker.

Fixed the Russian options menu. The help line under the View row showed broken letters because the menu cut a long Cyrillic line inside a letter, so it now holds the whole help text. The rows View, Game, People & Traffic and Interface and the values Simple and Advanced had no translation, so they stayed English in every language; they are translated now (machine translation).

Filled the texts that were still missing in all translations: the console and developer log messages, the credits line, the CB radio handles, the editor shape name and the Portuguese editor labels. Machine translation, NOT checked by native speakers.

Added Japanese, Chinese Simplified and Chinese Traditional translations of every text (menus, HUD, jobs, CB radio, subtitles, credits headings, level editor). Machine translation, NOT checked by a native speaker. The CJK glyph rendering is a separate job.

Made the game draw Japanese and Chinese letters. A language with a cjk line in its language.txt gets the glyphs of its texts drawn at run time from the Noto Sans CJK font (SIL OFL, ships with the game) into the in game text, front end and HUD fonts. Text wraps after any CJK letter. The names of the three languages show in every language. English and the other languages look the same as before.
Changed the credits line in all languages to say reDriver 2: Extended is on top of the REDRIVER2 source port by SoapyMan. The other languages got a fresh machine translation of the new sentence.
Fixed a damaged translation line that could crash the game.
Wrote into the README and the localizations readme that most translations are machine made and ship as they are, and that a native speaker can send corrections.
Added the photo mode colour texts to all 21 language files by hand: the new tabs, rows, tips, the 30 looks and the credits line.

Added its own message for a replay, demo or mission of a city that is not installed (before it said the level was damaged). Written by hand in all 21 languages. The message box was never looked at on screen.
Added the texts of the Auto Exchange (panel, prices, messages and the shady CB calls) in all 21 languages, written by hand. NOT reviewed by native speakers.
Added the texts of the Auto Exchange menu and the Pick List in all 21 languages, written by hand. NOT reviewed by native speakers.

sections.title: Performance and Stability
lines: Fixed a small memory leak in the setup when a city conversion fails.
Fixed replays reading the wrong spot at the edge of the map, with no effect a player can see.
Changed damaged car pack files and damaged override pictures to get refused instead of crashing the game, after 6 crashes found with damaged files.
Added a freeze report: when no frame has been drawn for 20 seconds, the game writes where it was stuck into the crash log.
Fixed a freeze in split screen when a player was far off the map with the police after him, the traffic search never ended.

Changed the game logic to run on a steady clock that catches up when a frame is late, the same for every number of players, and made everything the game times follow that game clock, not the number of frames drawn, so the frame rate can't change the game.
Fixed the random number generator overflowing after about 25 minutes of play, and made the model shift of a mission file checked against its range.
Fixed the game's random numbers starting a restart at a different place than a fresh start.
Fixed restarts keeping the old camera (look direction and position), bot counter and cop target, so the first cars and people that appeared were not the same as in a fresh start.
Fixed the wallet of player 1 keeping its trip counter and loose cents after a restart, the money itself stays.
Fixed a restart keeping the hour of the old game, it now starts the day clock again like a new game, so traffic and people follow the hour again.
Fixed a restart taking the lowered rush hour limit of pedestrians for the full setting.
Fixed the Havana ferry foam timer surviving a restart, which changed the Havana traffic.
Fixed cars of a new game inheriting waits and yields from the cars of the old game after a restart, and cleared the traffic yield timers at a level load.
Fixed racers keeping the dodge side of the old game after a restart.
Made the game rebuild the pad menu names only when a pad is plugged in or removed, not on every pad update.
Cut the number of graphics error checks to one per frame instead of one after every drawn piece.
Changed two math routines of the traffic (square root and multiply-divide) to run several times faster with exactly the same results.
Changed the traffic to look only at cars in the nearby grid cells instead of every car, same results as before.
Changed the game to refuse replay files whose sizes and tables do not fit the file, so a bad shared replay no longer crashes it.
Changed the sound code to refuse samples with no end, writes outside sound memory and broken sound bank tables.
Changed the mission loader to check header sizes before using them, and the mission text sum no longer overflows.
Changed the ladder position to clamp when a save is loaded, and the text saves to get written safely in one step.
Fixed texts from files being used as a format string in the menus, and replay names keep their full length.
Changed the music loaders to limit the XM header counts and check the bank sizes.
Changed the language file loader to end its text and check the file size.
Changed menu music and car sound WAV files to be safe to load: the decode is capped, the rate is limited and the format chunk is checked.
Changed the mod scan to stop following junctions and cap the number of files it reads.
Did a second round of safety fixes for song tables, language texts, mission messages and sound memory.
Fixed a level or model with a bad texture page number reading outside its data. It shows page 0 and logs once instead.
Changed the car to car collision test to only look at neighbouring cars, three times faster with the same results.
Changed the check between you on foot and the cars to skip empty car slots, same results.
Cut the graphics calls for the car shadows and the grass, they are set up once instead of on every draw.
Put the fog, colour grade, sun shadow and light values of a frame in one shared block, about 500 fewer graphics calls a frame.
Fixed the pause menu going round in circles on a menu made only of separators, and the modern pause menu now holds up to 128 rows with the right row selected.
Changed the out of memory message to name the real menu path (Options > Graphics Settings in the pause menu, Options > Graphics in the main menu), and the console texts are in all languages.
Freed 58 MB of memory by removing a leftover vertex cache of the old PlayStation layer.
Fixed the graphics memory of the old level staying behind when you travel to another city, a chain of four trips held 1 GB.
Fixed built cars leaving memory behind at every level change.
Freed the grass memory of a level when it ends, so a trip to another city holds much less memory.
Added a clean-up of the cache of the far city, with a setting for how many files to keep.
Changed the street life layer to start with small buffers, from 52 MB to under 1 MB with the same pictures.
Added a shader cache on disk so levels start faster, the first start builds it while the intro plays.
Fixed a crash when a mod car model file in a level folder is damaged or too big, the level's own model is used instead.
Fixed a hidden number overflow in the traffic driving code: distances to far points are now squared in 64 bit, so cars far from their control node see the true distance.
Fixed the traffic spawn distance check: it wrapped past 65535 units, so a far car could look near and block a spawn. It is 64 bit now.
Fixed the crash when typing 'weather rain' in the console. A bad 2D item is now logged and skipped instead of crashing. Tested In-Game: Functioning
Stopped the city cache from being made again for every weather, so there is one 200 MB file and a start in rain no longer waits for a 7 second bake.
Made loading a city you have loaded before quicker: Chicago went from about 4.4 s to about 3.2 s from the start of the game to driving.
Made a crowd of the new pedestrians much cheaper to draw. The picture is the same.
Removed a short stutter when a new pedestrian model plays a walk, run or idle clip for the first time.
Made the first-start shader build faster: the 21 programs compile in parallel and finish in about 2 s of work.
Made the first load of a city quicker: the time to driving in Chicago on a first start went from about 9.7 s to about 6.9 s.

Added the setting Pedestrian Detail (High, Normal, Low) for the Driv3r pedestrians. High is the old look, Normal and Low use simpler models at a distance and cut the cost per pedestrian by about 40 to 50 percent.
Cut the cost of the light streaks on the wet road: the GPU time of a wet night went from 2.05 to 1.77 ms.
Sped up the tree shadows by skipping the trees outside the shadow strip.
Sped up making the city map picture on the first load of a city: Chicago 1.8 s to 1.05 s, Vegas 4.8 s to 2.9 s.
Changed the movie player to skip a damaged frame instead of ending the game. Valid disc movies play as before.
Fixed demo recordings storing cars from slot 256 up as another car; they are skipped and logged once. Old demos read as before.
Split the game into a developer build and a release build with one compile switch. The release build has no test code and is smaller (7.15 MB against 7.58 MB).

Stopped the timer of the game from using part of a CPU core. It spun the last 2.5 ms of every tick, now it waits on a high resolution timer and spins 0.6 ms. The timer used about 12 percent of a core before and about 1.5 percent after. Frame rate and game speed stay the same. The sound and the music timing were not listened to.

Made the night lights cheaper on the CPU. The cone of every car beam was worked out with five trig calls per point, now once per light. Night frame part for the batch pass in the night test: 0.54 to 0.55 ms before, 0.39 to 0.41 ms after (day is 0.28 ms). Pictures are the same: night and rain night test scenes have 0 changed pixels, the chaotic night chase scene shows the same difference with the old and the new build. The PC was loaded by other tests during the runs.
Fixed an OpenGL error that was logged on the first start of the game
Fixed crashes when a mod or scene has a damaged picture or a zip file that blows up when opened.
Fixed a crash and an endless loop on a damaged WAVE sound file.
Added stack protection and checked string functions to the game and the setup. The load time with them was not measured.
Made the second start of a city a little faster by reading the car files on several threads.
Fixed the stop of up to half a second in the first frames after a load by building the shaders behind the load screen.
Made the black bars over the loading picture close 3 times faster, so a city loads a bit sooner.
Changed the first-start shader build to give the graphics driver 2 programs at a time instead of 4, so a first start into Chicago went from 10.9 to 9.0 seconds.
Fixed far away pedestrians throwing a huge dark patch of shadow over the street, which also cost speed.
Added a level validator, so a damaged level file can no longer make the game read outside its data. Normal levels load the same.
Fixed a damaged profile or garage save file with a very long line: the end of the line is no longer read as a new setting, the whole line is dropped. Checked by automatic tests,
Fixed the texture page unpacker reading past the end of a damaged car or night texture block. It now stops at the end of the block. Checked by automatic tests,

Fixed five crashes when a level file is damaged and has no road and region tables: the game now gets further before it stops. A damaged level can still crash later, it is not refused at load yet. Found by the damaged level fuzz test,

Went through the event files, the front end main file, the sound mixer, the jobs and the borrowed cars line by line and fixed what was clear. A mission that calls the Chicago truck event too often, or triggers an event with a negative number, no longer writes outside its tables. A replaced front end screen file (SCRS.BIN) with too many screens, buttons or a bad link can no longer crash the menu. A negative side volume no longer gives a broken sound pan, a sound driver without the reverb functions is skipped, the mod jobs file and respect.ini keep their numbers in range, a very long line in fares.txt is skipped as a whole, and a car model with a wrapped polygon count is refused. The simulation changes only add checks.

Added checks for numbers in mod and disc files that could write outside the game tables or crash it: route and junction count of a mission, a mission cut off short, car slot and event flag of a mission target, city texture pages, special car numbers, police light bar and horizon values, long engine sound file names, a texture override over 256 KB, the kerb count of a level, file names that point out of a level package, and a script that went on after an error. A bad value is ignored or the file is refused, with a line in the log. Checked by automatic tests,

sections.title: LEVEL EDITOR
lines: Level editor: the menu dropdown no longer clicks through to the buttons below it.
Level editor: a box select over original faces is instant now (it used to cast 600 rays).
Level editor: the green highlight shows every selected face, tinted and outlined.
Level editor: a piece whose outline passes within a few pixels of the cursor is picked even when the ray misses it.
Level editor: every colour follows the HUD theme (70s, PlayStation, Driver Menu, mod themes). VIEW > Next theme switches it.
Level editor: the piece list shows a thumbnail of each piece's texture.
Level editor: F1 opens the manual and the polygon keys are F2 / F3.
Level editor: HELP > Keyboard shortcuts lists every shortcut in one table, checked for clashes at start.
Level editor: the renderer's own debug keys (F3, F5, F6, Backspace) no longer fire while the editor is open.
Level editor manual: 21 pages, including a BUTTONS page per tab made from the UI (every button with its tip).
Level editor manual: pages for the menus, themes, importing, the mission maker and scenes. The same text ships as EDITOR_MANUAL.txt.
Level editor import: drop an .obj (with its .mtl and pictures) on the window and it is copied into the library and used.
Level editor import: drop a png / jpg / tga on the window to use it as a custom texture.
Level editor: CREATE > OBJ MODELS lists the imported models, with a SIZE setting.
Level editor: in FACES mode a lamp, sign or barrier lights up under the cursor.
Level editor: a click turns that lamp, sign or barrier into a piece you can move, turn, scale, copy or delete (before it could only be deleted).
Level editor: fixed a hitch of up to 0.8 s every few frames in cities with many hidden original faces (New York has about 23 000).
Level editor: picking the original face under the cursor now uses a spatial hash, so a pick takes 1 ms instead of 160 - 810 ms.

sections.title: SCENES AND MISSION MAKER
lines: Scenes: new story format made of comic panels (picture + caption, voice and music wav), title cards and avi clips.
Scenes: they are files at mods/<pack>/scenes/<name>/scene.txt. See tools/MODDING_scenes.txt and mods/_samples/Sample Scene.
Scenes: play them from Extras > Custom Missions, with the console command "scene <name>", or as the intro / outro scene of a custom mission.
Scenes: slow camera moves over a picture (move=zoomin ... pandown) and fades.
Scenes: a scene can continue with another scene (next=).
Scenes: a mission can continue with another mission (THEN MISSION), so you can build a story chain.
Scenes: seconds=hold keeps a panel until a button is pressed.
Scenes: Left / L1 goes one panel back.
Scenes: a damaged jpg picture no longer closes the game.
Scene composer: new SCENES tab in the level editor that builds scenes with buttons (pictures, captions, voices, music, clips, order, PLAY).
Scene composer: drop png / jpg / tga, wav or avi files on the window to add them.
Mission maker: new INTRO SCENE / OUTRO SCENE rows.
Mission maker: the start, goals, targets and destinations of the draft are drawn as labelled rings in the editor view.
Mission maker: new NEW / COPY / DELETE buttons for mission slots.
Mission maker: a line under the summary says what the draft still lacks (no start, no goal, tail without destination ...).
Mission maker: new STOP, SPEED and POLICE steps for custom missions.
Mission maker: new CAR DAMAGE row and slot titles.
Mission maker: browsing the mission slots no longer leaves empty drafts behind.
Mission maker: EDIT TEXT no longer crashes on a read only mod folder.

sections.title: CAMERA AND CONTROLS
lines: Photo mode takes the mouse: Tab shows the pointer, a click on a row changes it, the wheel steps, and there is a Take Photo button.
Photo mode: the left stick strafed the wrong way. Fixed.
Camera Views: Options > Camera Views (also in the main menu under Controls) chooses which of the 12 views the camera button cycles.
Camera Views default: 3rd person, bumper, hood.
The on-foot view is no longer carried into the next car.
Gamepad: the radio buttons come only from your bindings (Radio / Job: Previous / Next).
Gamepad: the shoulder buttons no longer change the station when they are bound to something else.

sections.title: CUSTOMIZER
lines: The Customizer takes the mouse: tabs, car / sound lists, paint swatches and wheel cells are clickable.
Customizer: new Sound tab to pick the engine sound of your car from every sound the game knows (Driver 2 cars and the sound sets of mods' carsounds folders). You hear it while you choose.
Customizer Sound tab: labels come from carsounds/names.txt, and the audition works while the game is paused.
The engine sound choice is saved with the car in garage.sav.
Car customizer (pause menu > Customize) now has three tabs: Car, Paint and Wheels. The camera shows the car at an angle and turns around it.
Customizer Car tab: every installed car in one list (this city, the other cities, Driver 1, packs such as Gran Turismo). Your car is swapped on the spot, no restart. Works in Take a Drive.
Customizer Car tab: cars that are not loaded are loaded as you scroll.
Customizer Paint tab: the paints of that car as swatches.
Customizer Wheels tab: thumbnails of 188 wheel designs, with finishes.
Wheel designs: the stock wheels of the four Driver 2 cities and of Driver 1, and the wheel shop of Gran Turismo 2 as a separate set.
The Gran Turismo 1 rims were dropped (too blurry).
Wheel files: game\wheels\d2.wheels, d1.wheels (made from the discs' levels) and gt2.wheels (made from a Gran Turismo 2 disc).
Customizer texts are in 12 languages.
Customizer: new Lights tab to move the built-in lamps of any car in the 3D view (mouse gizmo or keyboard).
Customizer Lights tab: add lamps (headlight, taillight, turn signal, running light, side marker, reverse, brake, fog) with a name, colour and size.
Lamp behavior can be always on, brake, gas, reverse, lights on, turn left / right or hazard.
Customizer: new Exhaust tab to move the exhaust pipe of any car in the 3D view and add extra pipes with their own scale and smoke start.
Customizer: the rim size of the wheels is adjustable.
Lamps and exhaust pipes are saved per car as text in the Core mod (cars\fx\<car>.carfx).
The converted Driver 1 cars and the wheel files are stored in the Core mod now (mods\reDriver 2 Extended Core\cars / wheels).
The paint, wheel design and rim size of every car you customize are remembered in your save (saves\<profile>\garage.sav).
They are put on the car again when you start Take a Drive or pick the car.

sections.title: SETUP AND PACKAGE
lines: Setup: the city map pictures are made by the setup now, so the game no longer builds them at your first visit to a city.
Setup: at the end of the install it lets the game build the map of every city (Driver 2 and the installed Driver 1 cities) in a hidden window, about a minute and a half.
Setup: the loading pictures of the Driver 1 cities get their map behind the city name.
Setup (reDriver_Setup.exe): everything the dev game makes from your discs is now made by the setup itself, nothing else needs to be installed.
Setup now makes the Gran Turismo 1 and 2 cars (with pop-up headlights, decals and race cars) and all engine sounds.
Setup now makes the Driver 1 / Driver 2 / Gran Turismo 2 wheel designs (Customizer Wheels tab).
Setup now makes the four Driver 1 cities (Take A Ride).
Setup: new rows for Gran Turismo and Gran Turismo 2 (EBOOT.PBP, .cue/.bin or .iso). The Driver 2 disc 1 is the template of the cars.
Setup also makes the loading pictures of the Driver 1 cities.
Setup: disc images may stay in a .zip or .7z archive (also both discs, also an archive with several images). The setup unpacks to a temporary folder and cleans it up.
Setup: .rar and other archive types get a message to unpack them first.
Setup: all new texts are translated into the 12 setup languages.
Setup: the Driver 1 PC cars no longer print a FAILED line for pc_player15. The 30 PC cars are made as before.
Setup: Nero images use the first data track (audio tracks are skipped).
Setup: the window follows the DPI of the monitor it is on.
The modder tools (tools\*.exe) are an optional separate download (reDriver_ModTools_<version>.zip) instead of being in the game package.
Players do not need the modder tools. The package is a third of its size (34 MB instead of 131 MB) with fewer antivirus false positives. The guides stay in the package.

sections.title: CARS
lines: Yellow Cab: without the Driver 1 disc the cab is the Driver 2 Bel Air repainted yellow with the checker band.
Yellow Cab: the project ships only the painted pixels (an overlay). The rest is made from your own disc.
Gran Turismo cars: lamps and badges set back under a bigger body panel (the taillights of many cars) are drawn in front of it now.
Cars with more than 255 vertices / polygons can be dented now (the dent lists are 16 bit).
The old 255 limit also overran the damage level table of models with more than 256 polygons. Fixed.
The setup converts every car of your Gran Turismo 1 and 2 discs into the packs (about 1700 cars).
The car catalog holds 2500 entries now.
Gran Turismo cars: GT1 engine sounds are taken from the disc into the car sound sets.
The car -> engine mapping is approximate (by redline). The RX-7 uses it.
Gran Turismo cars: car scale 0.135, ride height, and denting without the 255 vertex limit.
All real traffic now uses the full detail car model at any distance. The low detail model is only left for ambient cars.
The Car Detail Distance option is gone. The GPU cars make the full detail nearly free.

sections.title: CAR STREAMING
lines: Car streaming: the cars of the packs (Driver 1, Gran Turismo 1 / 2 ...) are a catalog. Cars of Driver 1 and the first cars of a pack are loaded at the start.
Car streaming: other cars load when traffic or the Start Car picker needs them, and are given up again (least recently used, never a car on the map).
Car streaming limits: up to 250 car models at a time (was 140), 1200 catalog entries (was 96), 1000 texture rows (was 250), 600000 car polygons (was 56000).
Fixed: car texture rows above 127 went negative (garbled cars when many cars were loaded).
New in a pack's cars\index.txt: kind=street|race|special (only street cars are traffic).
New in a pack's cars\index.txt: rarity=<weight> (default 10) and pin=1 (always loaded).
New developer variables: REDRIVER_STREAMCARS, REDRIVER_EAGERCARS, REDRIVER_STREAMCOPIES, REDRIVER_STREAMTEST.
The cars borrowed from the other Driver 2 cities stream as well.
Replays name the car of a player (not a slot), and the traffic pick no longer depends on what is loaded, so a replay shows the same cars.
The developer showroom loads every streamed car that fits.

sections.title: CITIES AND TRAVEL
lines: Driver 1 cities: Driver 1 cars in the traffic had oversized wheels hanging below the body, because the cosmetics file of a mod (BetterCars, for Rio) was laid over them. Fixed.
Driver 1 cities: mods no longer replace the cosmetics, denting and car models of a converted Driver 1 city.
Driver 1 cities: the Driver 2 cars of Rio (borrowed into the traffic) have their bodies and textures again.
Driver 1 cities: you get out of the car without a crash, and Tanner is in every city.

Driver 1 cities: the Driver 1 levels have no model of Tanner, so the converter adds his 16 body parts and his texture page to each city level. The setup does the same, taking RIO.LEV from your Driver 2 disc.
Take A Ride lists all eight cities in the new menu style: the four Driver 2 cities, plus San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami and New York when installed.
Take A Ride: the city is always the day level. The time of day is the clock.
Take A Ride: Driver 2 cities offer Day / Dawn / Dusk / Night. Driver 1 cities offer Day / Dawn / Dusk. Los Angeles is a night city and always starts at night.
Per city data (map, labels, streets, gas stations, jobs, car sounds, level edits) is keyed by a city id now, so the Driver 1 cities no longer share Rio's files.
Driver 1 cities: planar water reflections from the water pieces of the edit pack (a flat piece with a texture named water...).
Driver 1 cities: the game makes a map picture from the level data for every city. It is generated on the first start and nothing is shipped.
Driver 1 cities: Los Angeles road spikes fixed (instance chains in the converter).
Level edits of the pack (the hand made water, canal and bridge pieces, also for Havana and Rio) ship in the Core pack.
Travel: Pause > Travel changes the city without restarting the game.
Driver 1 cities run a day-only clock (sunrise to sunset).
Gas stations in Havana, Las Vegas and Rio. Street lights in Rio and the Driver 1 cities.
Driver 1 cities: pedestrians walk the pavements. Run the setup again to convert the cities and get them.
Driver 1 cities: loading pictures with the city name.
Driver 1 cities: no more invisible cars (wheels only).
Driver 1 cities: Los Angeles lighting fixed.
Driver 1 cities: per city settings in cities\<NAME>.ini / config\city_<0-3>.ini (day only clock, brightness, paints).

sections.title: TRAFFIC
lines: The car you got out of is no longer removed by the traffic clean-up (the jam breaker and the density trim skip it). It stays at the gas pump while you fill up.
Only the normal distance rule removes the car you left, when you are far away.
Traffic cars: the Gran Turismo cars no longer appear in the traffic. For now they are for the customizer only.
Developer Options > Traffic Cars: Extended. On = the cars of the level, of the other cities of Driver 1 / Driver 2 and of the car packs you switch on. Off = vanilla, only the level's own cars.
Developer Options > Traffic Cars: one row per car pack.

sections.title: POLICE
lines: Police: the backup respawn time is the original 320 (it was 170).
Police: the cops' speed and strength follow the felony like the original game (no Survival strength at the top of the bar).
Police: the default Max Chasing Cars is 4.
Police Options > Patrol Cars (None / Few / Normal / Many, default Few): sets how many patrol cars the traffic carries.
Patrol Cars: the old value was Normal. With the busy traffic that meant about three cops around you all the time.
Police backup cars never appear in view. They are born out of sight (a 70 degree cone ahead up to 240 m, and 70 m all round).
Police backup cars are born at least 7 seconds of your speed away, and never closer than 100 m.
Police backup cars have no collisions until they are close and the way is clear, and they wait while their nose is in a wall.
The siren of your own car (the horn of a car with a siren) now flashes the cop lights on the street.

sections.title: GRAPHICS AND LIGHTS
lines: Options > Graphics: new Exhaust Pipes option (the 3D pipe models).
Options > Graphics: new Tail Lamp Glow option (the red lens of the tail lamps lights up).
Options > Graphics: new Handbrake Brake Light option, off by default. With it off, the handbrake no longer lights the brake lamps (this was one of the reports).
Options > Graphics: View Distance now goes down to 1 (the original game's draw distance).
The flat car shadow (Sun Shadows off) is the static original one again. It no longer stretches away from the sun into a big block.
Sun Shadows is the dynamic shadow system.
Reflections and the other graphics tweaks apply to the day versions of all four Driver 2 cities.
The water reflects the sky and clouds.
The black rectangle around a wheel whose hubcap came off is gone.
GPU cars: a chrome reflection (streaky sky / horizon sphere map, added over the body and glass) on every car: Driver 2, Driver 1 and Gran Turismo cars.
Chrome reflection strength follows the Car Reflection option and dims at night. Developer variables REDRIVER_CHROME / REDRIVER_GTREFL set the strength.
Cars: the chrome reflection replaces the old world reflection on the car bodies (one reflection, not two). It also works with the CPU car path.
Lights: L switches the headlights of your car on / off at any time of day.
Lights: K = high beams (longer, brighter beams).
Lights: J (held) puts the left pop-up headlight down (a wink).
Pop-up headlights (Gran Turismo 2 Nissan 180SX) move up and down with the lights.

sections.title: SOUND AND MUSIC
lines: Driver 1 sounds: crash sounds of Driver 1 cars are the real crash sounds of the disc (light thud, crunch, heavy crash). They used to be the steel barrier and wood fence clangs.
Driver 1 sounds: engine and idle loops play at the pitch of the disc (the per kind tuning is gone).
Run the setup again with the Driver 1 disc to get the new Driver 1 sounds.
Driver 1 cars: the light hit keeps the Driver 2 sound (the Driver 1 sample used for it was the steel barrier clang).
The setup makes 528 sound sets from your own Gran Turismo 1 / 2 discs, with every loop of the engine bank.
New layered engine sound type: carsounds/<set>.layers + <set>_L<k>.wav crossfade up to 9 loops over the rev range like the Gran Turismo games.
Gran Turismo 2 cars play the intake and the exhaust bank together. The gear shifts of Driver 2 are heard.
The sound state (music tracker, channel timers) is changed under one lock now (rare sound glitches).

sections.title: PERFORMANCE
lines: GPU cars: car bodies, undersides, wheel arcs, wheels, damaged cars, cars lit by dynamic lights, car shadows (shadow map), the far ambient traffic and the civilian pedestrians are drawn by the graphics card from static buffers.
GPU cars: before, this was done polygon by polygon on the CPU. The look is the same.
GPU cars: about 50 % more frames in dense traffic on a fast PC, and much more on an old CPU.
GPU cars: new option Options > Graphics > GPU Cars and config.ini [game] gpuCars=1 (0 = the original CPU path).
CPU use: the game used almost two CPU cores (180 - 190 % of one core, in the main menu too).
CPU use fix: the thread sleeps until the tick now and the limiter waits on a high resolution timer.
CPU use result: about 80 % of one core in play, 30 - 50 % in the menus, same 160 fps.
Logic tick cost: the traffic passes look at the cars of the grid cells around a car instead of all 160 slots.
Logic tick cost: the integer square root and the 128 bit division of the traffic maths use a floating point estimate made exact by integer checks (same numbers).
Logic tick cost: the sound emulation decodes a car sound once instead of at every start (starting a car sound took 1 - 5 ms inside the logic tick).
Logic tick of a rush hour with 116 cars: median 0.55 -> 0.42 ms, 99th percentile 2.0 -> 0.8 ms, slowest 6.4 -> 1.2 ms.
The traffic behaves exactly as before.

sections.title: MODS AND MENUS
lines: The button tooltips are translated.
The shipped config.ini has overrideContent=1 (the content override of mods with car models is on).
Fixed: BetterCars (and any mod with a DRIVER2 folder: car models, .cos cosmetics) did nothing.
Cause: config.ini shipped overrideContent=0, which switched the mod content off after the mods had asked for it. The mods now keep it on.

sections.title: SAFETY AND FIXES
lines: Replays: the ping packets stored the car slot in a signed byte, so with up to 160 cars the slots above 127 read as negative numbers. Fixed.
Replays now store a fingerprint of the simulation settings (traffic, AI, police, physics mode) and of the mods.
The log says when a replay is played with other settings ("it may play differently").
Boats: the cars that ride on a boat were a 32 bit mask, so with 160 cars every car above slot 31 stood still while the boat moved, and Tanner's bit landed on car 0. A real bit set is used now.
Level safety: the model tables have 2048 slots (a cell object type is 11 bits), so a damaged or modded level cannot read outside them.
Fixed: reading a damaged / modded level could index outside the model and texture tables (barrier scan, roof scan, far renderer).
Running out of memory now writes the size and place into logs\log.txt, shows a message and closes the game instead of crashing.

sections.title: LOGS AND BUILD
lines: Logs: the developer trace log logs/batchlog.txt (about 130 KB appended on every start) is only written when REDRIVER_BATCHLOG is set.
Logs: the bridge piece list logs/bridgelog.txt is only written when REDRIVER_BRIDGELOG is set.
Logs: shader / framebuffer failures and the bridge summary go into logs/log.txt.
A normal run now writes only log.txt, the engine log and a few small files.
The shipped exe ignores the developer / test environment variables (REDRIVER_*, 326 of them: test beds, traces, cheats of the dev tools).
Still working in the shipped exe: the Travel restart and the documented options REDRIVER_D1COP, D1FILES, D1PC, KEEPBARRIERS, RADIODIR, NOFASTCARS, NODEFERPRESENT, NOBATCHCACHE, BATCHLOG.
Batch cache: at most 2 files per level (was 4) and 1.5 GB for all levels together.
Batch cache: unfinished .tmp files of a crashed write are removed.

versions.status: 2026-10-12   (RELEASED publicly 2026-10-12 - everything since 0.2.0 is listed here; the 0.2.1 - 0.2.8 test builds were never published)

sections.title: CARS AND DRIVER 1 CONTENT
lines: Driver 1 cars from the PC release now have one 16 colour palette for every texture of the car (not one for the whole page).
Driver 1 PC cars keep their smooth shading and have six paints (the real palettes of the release).
Driver 1 PlayStation cars keep their original colours.
All Driver 1 cars use the Driver 1 engine and idle loops, with three Driver 1 horns pitched by kind of car (cop, family, luxury, old, muscle, sport, small, truck).
Added the Driver 1 crash sounds (light, medium, heavy) and the Driver 1 tyre skid.
The setup builds these sounds from the disc (Driver 1 Sounds mod).
Driver 1 cities (Pause > Travel) are marked experimental: the ground heights of the converted cities are not right yet and cars can fall off hills where the data jumps. That work is on hold.
The map screen and the minimap of the Driver 1 cities now look like the Chicago map (red streets, grey land, green parks, pale blue water; finer picture, 256 world units per pixel).
Mods can bring extra cars (mods/<name>/cars/index.txt + .d1c files, made from a car content mod).
Extra cars from mods appear in traffic in every city.
New config key startCar (file name of a car): Take a Ride starts in that car.
New in Options > Gameplay Settings: Start Car, Start Car Paint (six paints for cars that have them) and Restart With This Car.
Pick any mod or Driver 1 car and its paint, then restart to drive it.
Extra cities (experimental): the four Driver 1 cities (San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, New York 1978) can be converted to Driver 2 format by the setup from your own Driver 1 PC disc.
To add one, drop it into <game or mod folder>\cities\<NAME>.LEV (+ .img map, .ini name / start / gas stations).
Extra cities appear in Pause > Travel (Take a Ride) next to Chicago, Havana, Vegas and Rio. Choosing one restarts the game into that city.
They have the real streets, buildings, hills, civilian cars, traffic with lights, gas stations and a minimap. The night uses the mod's night lighting.
Not there yet in extra cities: pedestrians, lit night windows, roadblocks, special cars, a loading picture per city.

sections.title: POLICE
lines: Half of the police cars (patrols, chase cars and backup) are now Driver 1 cruisers with a light bar and the Driver 1 siren; REDRIVER_D1COP=<percent> changes the share.
Police need a clear line of sight now: a building between you and a patrol car hides you (no felony, no pull-over, a chase can be lost behind a corner).
Patrol cars are part of the ordinary traffic again, also while you are on a taxi fare or another job (they were never added during a job).
Police cars driving around or parked at the kerb with the civilian cars are real patrol cars: they watch for offences, pull you over and join a chase.
At most two driving patrol cars appear near you at a time; parked ones do not count.
Fixed: a freeze when the police backup was placed on a junction or off the roads (an endless search for a road piece at a fixed position).
Busted: it needs the police to see you, two or more cars closing in, you standing still AND the car unable to move more than 10 m forward or backward (a vehicle in the lane or a wall).
Standing still, watching something or hiding is no bust.
Busted ends the game, like drowning or wrecking the car in a pursuit; there is no fine any more.
In Take a Ride the on screen messages (offences, police) are at the top of the screen instead of the middle of the road view.
Police chases: backup cars are called in at the original rhythm (see below for where they appear).
The 'Dispatch: backup is on the way' call-out is gone, because it gave you too much warning.
Police (Take a Ride), part 2: backup is called during a chase. Extra cars appear far out of sight as ghosts, race to you and turn solid once they are close and nothing is in the way.
Backup spawn rate is about 10 % faster than the original.
The police get faster, stronger and ram you more the higher the felony; the top of the bar feels like Survival.
Boxed in by the police at a standstill = BUSTED (fine, the chase ends).
Offences within three seconds count once (the worst one), and a stop adds them all to one ticket.
The felony bar shows the worst of them and is cleared after the stop.
New Offence Severity list: how much each offence adds to the felony.
Traffic stops: you have 10 seconds to reach the stop point (60-100 m ahead).
Blowing past the stop point, driving off or ignoring the stop starts a chase at half the felony bar.
The officer walks to your door, faces it and talks to you: he asks if you know why he stopped you and lists the real reasons.
You answer with a popup: left = aggressive, right = polite, doing nothing = neutral (Y / N keys or the d-pad).
Every answer is a real line. The neutral one is said when you press nothing and just keeps the conversation going.
A polite answer sways the officer towards a warning or a dropped offence.
An aggressive answer is for fun (name calling, snappy comebacks) and costs you leniency; real abuse (calling him a pig) turns the stop into a chase.
Many more lines of officer dialog.
When the stop is over the officer walks back to his car and gets in, and the normal traffic AI takes the car again (new route from where it stands, lane change around you when there is a lane free).
Police (Take a Ride): up to 6 cars chase you (setting, 2..12). The vanilla Take a Ride sent only the patrol cars that happened to be near.
A chase needs more felony now (Chase Threshold: Classic / Relaxed / Lenient / Very Lenient, default Relaxed).
Light bumps, scaring pedestrians and property damage get a traffic stop on a clean record, like speeding does (Pull-Over Offences: Extended).
The felony cools down by itself once the cops lost you (Felony Cool Down).
New Police list in Options (main menu and pause menu).

sections.title: TAXI, JOBS AND RADIO TALK
lines: Taxi: fares pay more at rush hour (dusk, +30 %), at night (+15 %) and in the rain (+25 %), and the dispatcher says so in the offer.
Taxi: VIP fares (a singer, a quarterback, the mayor...) pay two and a half times the meter.
VIP fares have rules: no speeding and no bumps, three strikes and they walk, a flawless ride earns a bonus.
Night shift: tipsy passengers change their mind about where they are going and may grab the wheel; a patrol car that sees it pulls you over.
Night shift: dodgy passengers may run without paying; stop next to them within ten seconds and they pay.
Taxi: any cab that spawns in traffic (Driver 1 cabs too) can be used for fares.
Taxi: the drop-off marker shows the street name.
Serial stories: passengers sometimes tell a long story (about two to three minutes a part, with several choices) that lasts the whole fare.

There are five serials with three parts each: a bakery that is not just a bakery, the treasure of Uncle Mort, the night clerk of a haunted hotel, a wife with a secret life, the caller on the night radio.
If the fare or the part ends in the middle, the dispatcher can call you again with the same passenger, who picks up where he stopped ("Now, where was I?").
Serial progress is saved (saves\default\fare_serial.ini).
Only crashes cost mood now (red lights and the wrong side of the road do not).
An average above 60 mph for fifteen seconds without a crash is the fast bonus.
Taxi passengers are much more forgiving: speed, hard braking and police chases no longer upset them.
Only crashes cost mood, and a passenger only walks out after a lot of them.
Smooth driving and fast, clean driving earn a bonus on the tip (up to +40 %).
Passengers start talking 8-16 seconds into the ride (they hardly ever told a story before).
The talk panel of a passenger has a plain green light instead of the police lights.
Fixed: answering a prompt with the d-pad (CB offers, the taxi dispatcher, briefings, the officer, the passenger's questions) also changed the radio station.
The d-pad does not touch the radio while a prompt is open or for a moment after it closes.

More talk variety (GTA-style satire, PG-13): about 1,170 passenger stories and small talks now (revenge of the pigeons, the man who sold a 'genuine antique', a sandwich-shop heist, the mime in the box ...).
Four new CB themes: the absurd, fake commercials, crackpots, neighbours.
CB chatter comes about every 45 seconds.
Job offers come 1-2 minutes after a pass or timeout and 3 minutes after you accept one. Taxi dispatcher calls are unchanged.
People and talk: everybody you talk to in person has a name now (fares, and the traffic stop officer, e.g. 'Officer Kowalski').
Names come from about 330 male and 220 female first names and about 790 surnames. The dispatcher tells you the fare's name.
Passengers no longer comment on every bump. Their mood about your driving only moves the tip, and they remark on it now and then; they talk to you instead.
About 780 stories and small talks have answers: left = aggressive (rude, funny), right = polite, nothing = a neutral line.
Stories fork on what you say, every story has random names, places, food ... filled in, and the last 330 stories are not repeated.
The CB radio is ordinary 70s civilian chatter (not truckers): 360 situations in ten themes (traffic, weather, food, family, work, fun, gossip, radio talk, shopping, car trouble).
CB situations have comments, closing lines and openers that combine into thousands of different messages.
There are thousands of callsigns like 'Lucky Pike' or 'Stockyard Sam', and the last 90 situations are not repeated.
Taxi, part 2: pedestrians on the kerb wave down the empty cab; stop within 25 s (setting Taxi Hailing).

TOUR fares (about one in five in Chicago): the tourist names a district, you drive around in it for about a minute, he names the next; after three districts you take him back to his hotel, with a tour bonus on the fare.
The roof sign of the yellow cab is lit while it is free, and the cabs in traffic light up now and then.
Taxi: a dispatcher now calls the fares on the CB radio with street name, distance, direction, length of the ride and the estimated fare.
Dispatcher keys: Y takes the fare, N passes; the next call comes in 15-30 s.
Turn the dispatcher off in Pause > Gameplay > Taxi Dispatcher to get the old self-starting fares.
Passengers watch your driving: bumps, hard braking, speeding, red lights, the wrong side of the road and the police on your tail get remarks, their mood drops and so does the tip.
A passenger who has had enough gets out without paying. A long smooth stretch is praised.

sections.title: TRAFFIC AND PEDESTRIANS
lines: Pedestrians can be run over: they no longer always run clear of your car. Some are distracted, most are alert but a fast car leaves little time; honking and slow driving still make everybody dodge.
When the body of your car hits a pedestrian he is thrown, tumbles, bounces and slides along the road, then lies there with limp limbs for about 20 seconds.
Hitting a pedestrian is an offence (hit and run).
Switch: Gameplay > Run Over Pedestrians (also in the front end Police list). Traffic cars never hit pedestrians.
Traffic: fixed the heavy-traffic gridlock.
Cars in slots 128-159 (only used above about 125 cars) never moved because their id was a signed byte. Fixed.
Confused cars and parked cars that could not pull out no longer block lanes or pop out of existence.
Cars waiting for a gap to turn across traffic accept shorter gaps the longer they wait.
Measured in Chicago with 150 cars: cars moving without the jam breaker went from 32 % to 79 %, and jam breaker removals dropped from 626 to about 60 in 2 minutes.
Traffic signals rebuilt: every signalled junction now serves one approach at a time (straight, right and left of that approach go together, everybody else is red), in turn.
Signal cycle: 15 s green, then amber, then a short all red, then the next approach.
During amber nobody new may enter and the cars in the junction clear it (5 s, ini key lightAmberSecs). The all red time is set by lightClearSecs.
All junctions share one clock and the lamps on the heads follow it.
Opposite left turners and crossing traffic never move together any more (near collisions between crossing cars at signals went from 12 to 0 pair-seconds in my traffic test).
Turning cars no longer stop half way across the junction.
Right turners no longer wait for a car standing in the opposite lane of the road they turn into.
Parked cars beside the exit no longer block junctions.
Cars no longer change lanes within about 2 s of a junction (neither before nor after it). Turns are not affected.
Traffic and pedestrian density now follow the time of day (ini [game] timeTraffic=1, 0 = always full).
Density by time: rush hour 16:00-18:00 is 95-100 % of the configured limits, 8:00 about 80 %, noon 75 %, midnight 35 %, 4:00 about 25 %.
Extra cars are taken away one per second while nobody can see them. The limits come back as the clock moves on.
AI cars can drive to a destination (road aware, shared route data, no per-car planning; ambient traffic is untouched).
Auto-drive now drives to the waypoint you set on the map.

sections.title: CONTROLS, PADS AND WHEELS
lines: Controller: the extra buttons of a pad (back paddles / M buttons, e.g. of the 8BitDo Ultimate 2) can be assigned to any action in the controller rebind menu; press the button when the row asks for it ('Extra Button N').
Extra buttons only work when the pad reports them to Windows; try its D-input / Switch mode if the 2.4G / X-input mode hides them.
log.txt has a [pad] line with the number of buttons the pad reports.
Racing wheels (experimental): a steering wheel with pedals works as a controller; see Options > Controls > Wheel Controls.
Wheel Controls: Wheel Support (Auto / On / Off), and you pick the steering, throttle and brake axes by moving them.
Wheel Controls: invert switches, sliders for steering sensitivity / dead zone / curve / smoothing, and a dead zone + curve for each pedal.
Wheel Controls: a live view of the input, and Export / Import of the whole wheel setup as a .wheel file (config\wheel profiles) to share.
Wheel buttons are bound in Gamepad Controls like any other button.
The brake pedal also reverses. The wheel does not press menu buttons.
Wheel force feedback is off by default (Wheel Controls > Force Feedback (Experimental)).
Force feedback gives a centring spring that grows with speed and cornering, a pull when the car slides, a rumble for skids and road noise, and a kick in collisions.
Force feedback has sliders for overall strength, centring, road and skid effects and collision jolts, an Invert Force switch and a Test button.
Force feedback needs a wheel that supports it through DirectInput. It has not been tried on a real wheel.
Gamepad: new option Gamepad Control Mode (Analog Controls / Digital Controls) in the controller settings of the main menu and the pause menu.
The pad is held in the chosen mode all the time (the sticks could be dead after a load until Start + Select); Start + Select now flips the option.
Fixed: the Y / Triangle button of a gamepad did not resume the game from the first pause menu (only Continue did). The keyboard keeps its old behaviour.
Controllers and racing wheels keep working while the game window is not in focus (alt-tab, second monitor, recording software).
Gamepad: new option Swap D-Pad And Left Stick (Controls). The d-pad steers like the left stick (digital steering) and the left stick presses the d-pad directions (cruise, map, radio, menus).
With Swap D-Pad And Left Stick on, the HUD hints show the stick.
Fixed: the keyboard had no reverse with the Modern controls preset. The down arrow brakes and reverses now, also with the classic preset, like the brake button of the classic layout.
Gamepad controls have a Preset row at the top (main menu Options > Controls > Gamepad Controls and the pause menu).
Modern Controls preset: triggers for gas and brake, separate reverse, d-pad functions.
Classic Controls preset: the original PlayStation layout (X gas, square brake / reverse, circle wheelspin, triangle handbrake, the shoulders and triggers as before).
Rebinding a button afterwards shows the preset as Custom.
Fixed: a burnout (the wheelspin button) no longer stalls at about 50 mph. The hand-over to normal acceleration used to be treated as a light touch of the analog trigger (20 % power).
Controls can be rebound in both menus: Options > Controls > Keyboard Controls / Gamepad Controls.
To rebind, select a row and press the new key / button / trigger. Esc cancels, Del unbinds, Reset To Defaults restores all.
Bindings are kept in config\controls.ini on top of config.ini.
Controls: new Gamepad Steering Sensitivity slider (25-200 %).

sections.title: MENUS AND OPTIONS
lines: Menus (main and pause): Graphics is sorted into groups with headings (Quality, Lighting & Shadows, Reflections, World & Sky).
Menus: the HUD options and the day / night options moved to Display, together with Subtitles.
Menus: Police Options (Cop Difficulty is its first row) is in the Options list.
Menus: every option list has group headings (Display, Controls, Sound, Police Options, the keyboard / gamepad / wheel lists and the pause menu's Gameplay list).
Settings are saved as soon as you change them; you no longer need to quit the game.
Pause menu: new Exit To Windows entry (it saves and asks first).
Pause menu: Mods and Language are in the main pause list.
Pause menu: Options has Cheats and Developer Options (was Debug Options) at the end.

Developer Options only holds engine and test settings now (time and weather limits, rendering internals, traffic AI tuning, far density, economy and career numbers, debug overlays, skip mission, reset tweaks).
Everything a player would use is in the normal Options lists, only once (no duplicates).
The version text is in the title row of the pause menu.
Credits: Extras > Credits lists the project lead, the contributors (logos, BetterCars, Driver2TextureFixes, the 1977 Caprice) and special thanks.
Special thanks go to the original REDRIVER2 team, the input prompts pack and Reflections Interactive.
Credits also list translators, the libraries used and a short notice, and are translated into all languages.
Widescreen: the 4:3 pictures of the original menus, the loading screens and the movies are stretched across a widescreen window.
Options > Display > Menu Pictures chooses Stretched or Original 4:3 with black bars. The main menu picture and the game itself are not affected.
Main menu: new ultrawide main menu picture (3440 x 1440).
Pause menu > Options > Credits shows exactly the same credits as the main menu (scrollable).
The pause menu shows reDriver 2: Extended with the version and the build time.
First start: the graphics settings default to the Max preset instead of my test values.
Max preset: view distance 400; reflections on cars / wet roads / glass / water at 80 / 70 / 60 / 80; dynamic lights.
The main menu picture (mainmenu.png) of the core pack now ships.
Menus: "Mods (restart to apply)" became Mods with a small sublabel; the same for Conflicts (main menu and pause menu).
Fixed: Cop Difficulty and Subtitles were also written to tweaks.ini and could disagree with the profile. They are stored in the profile only now.
The pause menu can now be opened in the free camera too (not while the level editor is active).
Main menu: new Extras screen (Replays, HighScores, Secrets).
Secrets is one list: Mountain pass, Race track and Bonus gallery (the original secret screens, available without earning them).
Secrets also has toggles for invincibility, police immunity, player ghost, puppy dog cops, mini cars, Jericho mode and secret car.
Secrets has Unlock Everything (all missions, cutscenes, secrets and secret cars; saves the profile).
Options lost HighScores; Gameplay lost Controller and Vibration (Vibration moved to Controls, next to gamepad steering).
Main menu picture override: a PNG named mainmenu.png in a mod folder (or the game folder) replaces the main menu picture.
The picture can be any size and aspect ratio (for example 16:9 or 21:9 with a new logo). See tools\mainmenu\README.txt.
Options reorganized (main menu and pause menu): Display, Graphics, Controls, Sound, Gameplay, Language, Mods.
Display holds the graphics preset (Low / Medium / High / Max), window mode (windowed / borderless / exclusive full screen), resolution, FPS limit and VSync.
FPS limit choices: 25 / 30 / 50 / 60 / 100 / 120 / 144 / 165 / 240 or unlimited.
Display choices apply at once and are remembered in config\display.ini.
The preset changes view distance, reflections, shadows, grass, lights and so on in one step. It shows Custom when you changed a single value.
The main menu now has the same lists as the pause menu.
Sound: the main menu Options > Sound is now a list with SFX, music and radio volume (same list in the pause menu). The radio volume is remembered.
New sound mixer sliders, each 0-200 %: your engine, traffic engines, horns and sirens, tyres and skids, collisions, ambience and weather, voices, pedestrians and footsteps.

sections.title: HUD AND MAPS
lines: The tachometer lost the second dark plate behind the digital speed.
HUD messages (offences, police, mission messages) are drawn as a plate in the style of the top HUD panels, instead of yellow letters over the road view.
The message plate hangs under the objective / traffic stop panel when there is one, so it no longer overlaps it. The classic HUD keeps the old text.
HUD: the money is in a pill, moved clear of the fuel gauge.
HUD: the d-pad hints under the map show all four directions (Cruise = up, Map = down, Radio = left / right for previous / next station).
Left / right on the d-pad also answers a job offer, shown with the single left + right icon.
HUD: the damage and wanted bars are brighter and further from the map, so their icons no longer touch it.
HUD themes: Options > Display > HUD Theme switches between Modern 70s (walnut and orange), PlayStation (navy glass, steel bevels, Driver red and yellow) and Driver Menu.
Driver Menu theme looks like the main menu's option lists: flat translucent black panels, yellow headings, a dark red selection bar, no stripes, flat gauges and hint pills with a thin red rim.
Menu Style (Display) chooses how the pause menu looks, independent of the theme: as the theme says, a centred window, or a translucent side panel like the main menu's lists.
The Driver Menu theme uses the side panel.
Modders can add HUD themes as text files in <mod>\hud\themes\<name>.ini (name, ten colours, accent, corner roundness, bevel, menu, stripes, hud); see mods_README.txt.
HUD: the Driver Menu theme uses muted colours like the original release, more transparent panels and no bar on the hint pills.
Driver Menu theme: the red of the original minimap border is used for the rims and thin lines (map rim, tachometer rim, the line of the side panel menu).
The dark disc behind the tachometer is off by default; Options > Display > Gauge Background switches it on.
HUD: the three controls pills under the minimap are now a Controls hints panel (Cruise, Map, Radio, with the keys or the d-pad / stick icons).
The Controls hints panel pops up at the top right when a game starts and again every 10 - 15 minutes for ten seconds; Options > Display > Hints turns it off.
The minimap moved down to the height of the speedometer.
